“Good. Because I expect it would be dark inside of a trunk, and then I wouldn’t be able to
read along the way.”

Gerion chuckled.

“Now. Is it more effective for you to go by yourself, or should you go with Aunt Genna?”

“Oh, good,” Gerion sighed. “I thought I’d have to work very hard indeed. But if you’ve
convinced Genna to ask, then it would be much easier. Why, I probably won’t even-”

“No, Uncle, I need the both of you! You said you would!”

“Very well,” Gerion stood up. “I suppose we should see how she wants to go about it.”

“Oh, excellent. Dinner at Aunt Genna’s. Or perhaps not? If you look at Emmon and start
laughing, I don’t know that it would help my cause.”

“Me?” Gerion pretended to be wounded. “What about you?”

“I shan’t laugh. I’ll be too busy looking anywhere but him. I never look him in the eye
anyway. Too short, you see, I just end up staring at that bobbling apple in his throat and
wondering how it is possible that it sticks out further than his chin!”

“Now- Tyrion-” Gerion fell into a new round of laughter. “Now you’ve ruined it! I simply
can’t look at him now!”

Tyrion’s pleased smile at succeeding in making Gerion unable to even walk forward from
laughter warmed Gerion’s heart and made him laugh even more. It was always seen as a
disgusting failing in Tywin’s eyes, that Gerion would whoop and cackle, chuckle and giggle
at the slightest provocation and worse, turn red and short of breath if sufficiently amused. It
was too much like their father, Tygett cautioned him once as a child, unable to understand
why his eldest brother once turned on him with a snarl and yelled at him until he was in tears.
You must not smile so around him.

Gerion tried to be good and obey, until Tywin gave the order to Tygett to marry Lady
Darlessa Marbrand. Tygett carried a torch for a Farman maid, but Lord Farman displeased
Tywin and he certainly would not reward that House with a Lannister marriage after that.
Gerion watched helplessly as Tygett vomited in hung over misery the moons leading up to
the wedding, and drank some more, heartsick. He was ill looking when the wedding
happened, Gerion remembered, but ever the dutiful brother and knight, went through with it.

So to be good gave you no satisfaction and Gerion resolved to not bother trying after that.
Tywin was going to ruin his happiness somehow, someday. So why hold back his laughs now,
when he would have no reason to laugh later?

After all, once Tygett did his duty and fathered Tyrek, no other children were forthcoming,
were there? There was nothing particularly wrong with Lady Darlessa and Tygett treated her
with courtesy, but there was no love there. Certainly Tygett avoided her when he was in his
blacker moods so as to not frighten her and would seek out Gerion’s sympathetic company
for drinking. And for a time Tyrion joined in and they made quite a scene at the Lannisport
whorehouses, to the point of causing Tywin to come down upon them like a mineshaft
collapse.

He was wroth and made even more so when Gerion laughed.

Now, as he walked beside Tyrion at his pace, he thought that the laughter that had somehow
gone missing from his nephew was back and he was glad. He had worried at first, when
Tyrion seemed all at once to have shut himself up inside the Casterly castle; was this some
sort of self imposed exile? But no, Tyrion was not taking a novel form of rebellion against
Tywin; he was busy and nobody knew what he was doing. He began collecting different
rocks being discarded from the mines and books began to be moved from the library and he
disappeared from the main dining hall, taking meals alone, unless it was the dinners where
Tywin expected everyone to show up, just so that he could preside over them in judgement.

Tyrion tried to situate himself besides him or Tygett these times. Gerion found himself
charmed when Tyrion showed him a quartz and began explaining all the different things he
found out about the quartz. Gerion never knew that the rock within the mines was hard
enough to resist scratching with steel.

“If that is so, then how do the miners break it up?”

“It is because resisting a scratch doesn’t mean it can resist getting hit hard enough to shatter,”
Tyrion quietly said, to avoid Tywin’s attention. “Just because something is hard does not
mean it is also not brittle. Like the difference between iron and steel, you see?”

Tygett and Gerion raised their eyebrows, having never thought of it before.
Gerion did learn more sorts of seemingly useless facts, but he supposed that a Lannister
becoming obsessed about knowing the properties of the Rock was somehow acceptable. He
did not think further on it, preferring to live day by day, avoiding Tywin and putting off
obeying his orders until unavoidable. He supposed that Tyrion was becoming the same way.

But today, he found that Tyrion still wanted things. Still wanted things enough to scheme for
them. He didn’t suppose there was much hope of success and he almost wanted to tell Tyrion
to give up. After all, Tyrion tried so hard on this sixteenth nameday to get Tywin to allow him
a tour of Essos for naught.

Finally, they reached a level within the Rock where there were servants posted and Gerion
told them to summon litters for him and Tyrion. Tyrion looked at him gratefully and it hurt
Gerion all over again. Of course no servants would disobey a Lannister. But Gerion knew,
everyone knew, that when Tyrion requested to be carried with a litter, the servants would take
their sweet time, until Tyrion was late and it was on purpose, because it was known that
Tywin… would prefer to have his son… inconvenienced. It was a form of spite that Gerion
had come to expect of Tywin and Tyrion was finally jaded enough to not bother asking.

This time, however, they were carried very efficiently to Genna’s apartments. They entered,
Gerion gave Genna a hug and Genna pinched Tyrion’s cheeks. Tyrion had long given up on
getting her to cease doing so. They went to the dining room and Emmon was there already at
one end. Cleos had married and he was with his wife in their own newly appointed living
quarters. That left Lyonel and Tion to join them at the table; Baby Walder was with his wet
nurse.

Tyrion politely greeted Emmon, who stared peevishly at him in faint disbelief before greeting
him back. Gerion bit the inside of his cheek. He did the same for his cousins and they
responded with rote disinterest in him. Gerion and Tyrion took the seats immediately to the
right and left of Genna at the other end of the table, leaving the sons to speak with their father
or not for the meal.

Genna was not moved to speak about the weighty matter of attempting to convince Tywin
until past the main course, which was roast sucking pig with sauce. She would not have her
enjoyment of the crisp skin and juicy meat curtailed by talking about Tywin. Gerion was glad
for it. Eventually, they were well and stuffed and Genna told Emmon and her children to
leave.

Tyion finished his wine and put the cup down, before he smiled at Genna with the attentive
air of a cat watching an unwary bird fluttering just out of reach.

“No sense dithering,” Genna chuckled. “Is there? Well. The fact of the matter is that Cersei
has been less than useless to Tywin at court. And if one is useless to Tywin, they are also
useless to the rest of us.”

She picked up a candied orange peel from a dish of sweets and put it in her mouth.

“I dare say that if Kevan and Tygett wanted Lancel and Tyrek placed at royal court, they
might as well go themselves, to hunt and jape and dance their way into King Robert’s favor
and make that ask. Seeing as Tywin won’t. But why injure his precious dignity, when we
have you?”

“Would I be that useful?” Tyrion asked doubtfully.

“Things have changed since Joanna’s day,” Genna replied, choosing another candy. “I’ve had
to have letters from Marbrand cousins to know. Cersei does not write. I can’t imagine why
not; it's not as if from the reports that she does anything of note at all! Corruption is being
sniffed out, and Targaryen loyalists and incompetents resting in sinecures are firstly having
their wrongs called out in the streets, and if very egregious, they are paraded through the
streets so that the smallfolk may have their fun throwing rotting vegetables at them, and then
gotten rid of; Wall, complete confiscation of properties, or worse. Entire positions are being
removed as obsolete or useless past Targaryen favor.”

“Yes, I’ve had news to that affect,” Tyrion nodded. “It is the Florents behind it. Strategic.
Wouldn’t do to have vulnerabilities within the Red Keep.”

“Which I do not begrudge. But I don’t know what Cersei’s been doing! I ask if there are any
likely openings, and she writes that I should submit names that Tywin would approve of, I do,
and then… Nothing! Nothing at all!”

“... I might know a bit about that.”

“Do tell.”

“As one would expect, Stormlanders are afforded first round pick,” Tyrion gestured. “Then
the now very frightened, grasping Crownlanders.”

“Not surprising.”

“Yes. Valemen and Reachers after. We are not being snubbed, but I’ve been told that courtiers
who think only to feast and do nothing useful are not welcome. You should know that lords
who can do no more than sign their name are not welcome. Full literacy only.”

“Full literacy.”

“Full literacy. Positions’ duties are being codified. Laid out neatly in lists. Responsibilities,
requirements and appointed persons must first demonstrate that they know their business, in
the form of summary reports of their own experiences, in their own hand, with written
references, if at all possible, by persons not related to them. They must make argument on
why they ought to have such positions.”

“... Stannis Baratheon never sailed a ship prior to his brother’s orders,” Genna frowned.

“But he can read and write. And they say that if the King appointed him to any other role, he
would have risen to the occasion, because he’s just that sort of paragon of duty. Granted,
everyone with sense is glad he’s not Master of Entertainments and Ceremonies, but there it
is.”

“... Tywin would approve,” Gerion reluctantly ventured. “Wouldn’t he?”
“Casterly Rock can afford to have some useless hangers on,” Genna shrugged. “Though the

exciting in the Red Keep.”

“The Florents are fun,” Tyrion smiled. “Have you heard of that new sport, with the horses?
Hammerball, they told me. They just have the knack for entertainment.”

“Now that’s what I mean,” Genna pointed her finger. “You have a most useful friendship with

“... Just because I am friends with the Florents.”

“Well, yes. Cersei certainly has not made friends of them. Granted, they should be trying to

“Definitely not,” Tyrion agreed. “They just happen to not be the usual court bootlickers.”

“And they are all proper graciousness and humility! They are not high in the instep at all!

her, they make her days lighter with song and japes and no wonder, that poor woman’s had

attended to her instead.”

Tyrion’s smile became a trifle false, thinking on the various letters from Selyse and Delena
criticizing his sister’s first instincts to be arrogant and free with her snubbing.

“Well. Cersei is a true lioness of the Rock. And Queen. She expects due obeisance.”

“That may be. But what about us? She must needs bring the rest of us to the hunt. What has
she done? Nothing. Had she gained the Florents and the other Reacher ladies onto her side,

And Genna narrowed her eyes cannily to Tyrion.

“I take that your friends advise the King and Lord Hand on appointments? Bring in Reachers

“They serve as sieves for competence and faults,” Tyrion confessed, since his Aunt was so

course of action. He wants to outshine Jahaerys.”

“Well. That’s just the sort of ambition a Baratheon would have,” Gerion chuckled.

“And you would say to Father that I would serve Casterly Rock’s interests better than
Cersei?” Tyrion sounded skeptical.
“I expect you can do better than uselessly nagging King Robert into taking Lancel and Tyrek

“Well. It would more likely cause him to do precisely the opposite out of spite. The Florents

Genna took on a faraway look.

“Extraordinary. Steffon was like that, you know. Remember, Gerion? He had a laugh that

Genna flipped her hand in the air.

“Huff and puff and smile and all of a sudden the sun came out from behind the clouds. Yes, I

“Your aunt,” Gerion, leaned forward towards Tyrion. “Would have preferred a chance of

“... Really?” Tyrion raised his eyebrows.

“Of course!” Genna straightened and patted a braid of her hair. “Wasn’t I a beauty in my day?

Genna sighed.

“Well. Not here to talk more of father’s foolish mistakes. You know the royal court very well

“Lord Renly writes to me as often as the Florents,” Tyrion volunteered. “And Lord Stannis

“Now, see that? Very, very good, Tyrion!”

“Now what is the use of me,” Gerion said self deprecatingly. “Tyrion, it is as I thought;
Genna has it all in hand.”

“You,” Genna reached over and patted Gerion’s hand. “Will go to Tywin and act as contritely
as you can and mouth words about wanting to be useful. At court.”
“Me? What? Useful? Genna!”

“Do stop whining,” Genna sniffed. “Have a candy.”

“Mmmpf,” Gerion didn’t dodge as Genna shoved a sugared plum into his mouth.

“It’s all well and good that Tyrion could put the idea of Lancel and Tyrek’s future squiring
forward with Lord Renly and Lord Stannis. But the King. The King loves hunts and that

Not our Tyrion. This stag takes two lions put to the chase.”

“... I understand,” Gerion sighed.

“And think, perhaps you gain a place at royal court for yourself and then you need not return

“I do hope that I wouldn’t be too important,” Tyrion mused. “I have work to do here, after
all.”

“That may or may not be. What you want is a chance to see that ship launch,” Genna smiled.
“And we shall make that happen.”

The next day, Genna used her position of most favorite (only) sister of Lord Tywin Lannister
to great effect, sweeping in with Gerion trailing in her wake, blithely ignoring any business
that Tywin might have. He pursed his lips disapprovingly at her from behind his desk, but she
chortled and peremptorily took a seat and Gerion followed her example (he always waited to
have Tywin’s permission to sit, but this was Genna’s hunt, so he followed her). She kept a
fixed, self-satisfied smile on her face and settled in to wait. Tywin doggedly continued his
writing. Gerion began counting backwards from a hundred in increments of three.

Finally, Tywin looked up to see Genna smiling at him still and dropped his pen.

“Well. What?”

“Is that any way to greet me?” Genna lifted her chin. “I must take it that your work is
troubling, for you cannot but be pleased to see me!”

Tywin narrowed his eyes at Genna and then looked at Gerion. Gerion attempted to seem as
unaffected as Genna, but he was once told by Tygett in the past that his face took on the air of
a dog caught stealing food off the table and it was not the look of a knight. Gerion cleared his
throat.

“What,” Tywin did not change the tone of his voice. “is the cause of your visit?”

“Gerion will be going to the ship launch.”

“...Yes! Yes. Ahem. Yes.”
Genna made a movement under her skirt and Gerion was suddenly glad that he was sitting far
enough away that she couldn’t kick him.

Tywin blinked.

“I. Uh. I believe that I could be useful at the royal court. At the least, see to getting those
squireships that Kevan talked about? For Lancel? Remember? Of course you do, and Tygett,
too, though Tyrek is full young to consider it, but you were a page at the Red Keep and they
could be pages to start and-”

“Cease. Babbling.”

Tywin sat, with his hands on his desk, motionless. Staring at him. Gerion’s eyes were starting
to go dry.

“Why him?” Tywin’s eyes switched to Genna.

“He’s doing nothing useful here. Not with Kevan and Tygett with full duties. King Robert is
known to be active and has reduced his time spent hunting in favor of all sorts of
horsemanship sports in addition to his schedule of sparring. Gerion would suit, I think, and he
has the charm that would do us good stead at court.”

“You think so?”

“Oh, yes!” Genna nodded. “Do let Gerion go and try. Give him something to do!”

Gerion tried to look eager. And dutiful. Dutifully eager. Uh. Good thing Tygett wasn’t there,
if he was, they’d look at each other and Gerion would ruin it by laughing.

“You will find suitable placement for your nephews at court. Do not take overlong at the
task.”

Gerion nodded quickly.

“And Tyrion will go as well,” Genna said.

“No.”

“Tywin.”

“I need him with me,” Gerion interjected.

Tywin’s nostrils flared and Gerion had to jump in while he was taking his breath to castigate
them.

“I shall require further introduction with the Florents. Through Lady Selyse, I shall have
cause to be invited to know Lord Stannis. Which means Lord Renly, as well, see? Which is
direct connection with the King. Remember what a good time the Florents had here, last they
came to visit? Surely they would be so good as to return the favor and issue me an invitation

by Tyrion and he would be so eager to help me at my task! They must think well of me if

“You do not actually require that little stump’s assistance to gain entry into court. Cersei is

“But she is no friend of Lord Stannis or Lord Renly and the King, unfortunately for us,

supported Gerion.

“Gerion is capable of obtaining the proper introductions and society on his own.”

“He would be starting with nothing. Tyrion is friends already with Lord Renly, at the least! Is

“I will write and instruct Cersei to make effort with her goodbrothers.”

“That’s precisely the problem,” Genna stoutly rejoined. “That you should need to tell her

Jaime. Tyrion.”

“One doesn’t go to war with the army you wish, but the army you have,” Gerion tried. “I

“We need this,” Genna pressed.

“I need the King to be well disposed towards me through Tyrion. And then, you can depend

“Very well.”

Gerion did not clap his hands like a child getting candy. Genna patted his hand and palmed a
candy to him that way.



They made good time to King’s Landing.

Gerion found himself and Tyrion subjected to a strangely uncomfortable dinner with just
Jaime and Cersei to themselves. Of course, he expected that Cersei planned it so that
everybody else knew of the exclusivity of her choice and would therefore be eaten up with
envy. But it was not enviable, how she made that brittle smile at Tyrion in greeting before
consequently ignoring him for the rest of the evening. Gerion hated sullen silences and threw
himself into the conversational fray, making Jaime laugh with his jests and getting Tyrion to
join in. As Tyrion wanted to try his best so that Gerion would succeed at court, he was
looking to be pleased and amused and managed to ignore his sister ignoring him. Together,
they plied Jaime with stories and anecdotes and questioned him about his duties with the aim
of gratifying his vanity over his position as a Kingsguard.

Jaime was so well pleased about Gerion visiting that he took his uncle out to practice at
Hammerball. Every knight who could not manage the skill to get a spar with the King wanted
to show off at Hammerball. It was the thing to do.

They got up earlier than Gerion would have liked, but he was ever easy to the will of others,
so he went when the sun was barely risen, putting his horse through its paces. He went
through pivots about one foreleg and then the other, and was concentrating so hard at keeping
control of his mount that he missed others entering the training yard and observing.

The tall, strapping youth with the black hair and bright yellow jacket with the black
embroidered antler racks on the upper arms must be Lord Renly. Gerion waved and Lord
Renly smiled and waved back. This was a good start!

They eventually formed a pick up game of other newcomers and it was just Gerion’s luck,
Stannis Baratheon was there too! As the brothers were regulars at the game, they removed
their jackets to reveal cotton shirts with turned down collars that buttoned partway down the
front with short sleeves, in bright yellow. It seemed that they were well prepared for the
rigorousness of the exercise, along with their mounts; braided tails and the manes trimmed
short in the name of avoiding risks of entanglements. They also strapped on simple helmets
and Gerion looked to Jaime.

“I’ll get you one to borrow, Uncle,” Jaime called out, waving down a servant.

Gerion followed after the Baratheons and stripped down to his shirt.

The game started in due course and Gerion found it quite refreshing. He missed his swings
more often than not, but the lack of danger from his horse stumbling on rocks or sudden
hidden drops in undergrowth made the activity much more fun than going on a hunt. His arm
was pleasantly sore, a sign of good effort and he even thought his whole body would ache
even after sleeping at a reasonable hour that night, because he had not had to gallop pell mell
in such a long time. In the end, his team lost against the team with the Baratheons, but it was
well.

They began walking the horses around the perimeter of the field to cool them down.

Lord Renly was welcoming and mentioned Tyrion and Gerion was glad to speak of him. He
was so absorbed and making pains to be agreeable and good company to be worth his
introduction that Lord Stannis’ suddenly raised voice startled him.

“What do you mean?” he snapped.

Gerion looked around.
Some Rambton knight was the focus of Lord Stannis’ glare.

“I said,” the man said in an overly informal tone. “Would that I could make my wife attend to
me a noon as you make yours.”

Gerion glanced to his side, at Jaime. Jaime’s face had went to stone.

“I don’t make my wife do anything,” Stannis said impatiently. “You are mistaken.”

“... Oh, we are all men here,” the knight continued. “You cannot mean to continue the
mummery that nobody knows about how you make your wife lay with you at noon. A
goodly, obedient wife, she is!”

“I repeat this just once more,” Stannis’ jaw worked. “I do not make my wife do anything.
You cease saying so.”

They stared at each other in mutual confusion.

“You mean to deny that she lays with you near every noon?” the knight scoffed.

“No. What-” Stannis’ already thin lips thinned. “Ah. I see.”

Stannis tilted his head.

“It’s because you are bad in bed. That you must make your wife. I am not. So my wife goes
to me out of her own desire.”

All conversation between everybody was silenced and Gerion felt an embarrassed laugh
tickling its way in his belly. No, no, he must hear this out, he can’t-

“I say, my lord, that’s uncalled for! I am not-”

“You are bad in bed,” Stannis remorselessly continued, his voice a carrying rumble. “My
sympathies to your wife.”

“HAH! Hah-hah!” Gerion couldn’t help it; it came out more a squawk than a leonine roar but
the effect was enough; the knight reddened.

“I-”

“No. That is not in question,” Stannis went on. “Let it be known lest there be any confusion;
women don’t have time for a one minute man. A two pump chump. A dull bore that makes
the evenings yet one more chore. A woman does not want to close her eyes and start taking
pantry inventory during the act.”

Gerion was bent over his saddle, futility clutching at his sides. He was sure he sounded like

   The Ironborn convoy paused on a hillcrest to take in the view of the Red Keep and King’s
   Landing. Rodrik smelled King’s Landing himself, years ago. It’s changed. None of that acrid
   bite of piss or the smack your face miasma of shit. It smelled like a proper seaside city; some
   rotting fish, the sweat of unwashed masses, of cooking fire smoke, with a tang of metal from
   the Street of Steel. They were met outside the Dragon Gate with a glittering troop of Gold
   Cloaks.

   They were escorted with proper pomp and ceremony, banners flying in the wind, horns
   sounding to clear the way, for a visiting Lord Paramount heir all the way to the Red Keep.

   Rodrik looked critically at the crowds of smallfolk that they passed by. They looked well-fed
   and they moved with purpose along the streets. They formed crowds, wanting to catch a
   glimpse of nobility, no matter that they were Ironborn. Rodrik and the other Harlaws took the
   time to toss coppers as they went. The others looked askance, but if there was anything useful
   he learned from his Harlaw cousins and from his lessons at his fathers and uncles, what with
   their tendency to attempt getting greenlander brides lawfully, was that greenlander nobles
   made shows of generosity because it made them popular and showed an enviable elegance of
   being. They made their way to the Red Keep and were shown their apartments for the
   duration of their stay and given time to refresh themselves and prepare for the feast.

   There was enough time for Alekyne Florent to stop by for a short visit before the expected
   feast, they were the guests of most importance. Rodrik was glad to reestablish their friendly
   acquaintance. As Rodrik did not need so much time to get ready as Lanny and Yara’s
   primping and fussing, he followed Alekyne to the Great Hall, where King Robert and the
   Lord Hand were holding court, with the Lord Hand. Court sessions were shorter; the Small
   Claims Court of King’s Landing did its job well in diverting petitioners to the bureaucracy
   answerable to the Master of Laws. At the moment, an emissary from Myr was speaking.
   Alekyne’s expression sharpened and Rodrik watched him absently rubbing his palms together
   as they stood in the shadows and listened.

   Interestingly, King Robert cut in during a moment of Lord Hand Arryn attempting to mollify
   the emissary putting forth the claim that Myrish glass-making guild trade secrets were
   somehow being stolen.

   “You can sail right back across the Narrow Sea with that!” he boomed out. “So you are
   threatened by Westerosi glassmakers improving at their craft. You’ll lose out on trade. Glass
   gets broken transported over the sea, raising your costs and risking your ventures. All very
   understandable. But to accuse Westerosi of theft!”

   He did not bang his fist on the Iron Throne, mindful of the risk of cuts. He waved his fist with
   emphasis instead.
“Good, honest Westerosi glassmakers do not steal! Whatever better quality and craft of glass
occurs in Westeros, it is because of study, experimentation, and being too stubborn to give up

There was a smattering of applause from the courtiers at this piece of patriotism. The
emissary frowned.

“Your Grace’s confidence in your people is most admirable-”

“You will not go sniffing around the guilds,” Robert replied firmly.

Lord Hand Arryn looked uncomfortable with how Robert was voicing his opinions. Robert
then settled a glare at the emissary.

“Must I also add that should any Westerosi guild members, journeymen, or apprentices or
their family members suddenly go missing or die from a bout of convenient gut sickness,
there will be consequences to you and yours?”

The emissary suppressed a wince at such rude Westerosi bluntness, entirely shocking to
Essosi sensibilities. He exchanged dismayed looks with his compatriots beside him, at a loss.

“I trust that the existing docking fees, gate fees, handling fees, and etcetera, being applied to
all ships entering King’s Landing’s harbor, as established by the previous regime and
continued by my current reign in the name of continuity and peace remains acceptable to
Myr’s glassmaking guilds?”

King Robert looked overly ready to begin a trade war. The Myrish contingent shuffled their
feet. This King was fresh off a victory on the Iron Islands. It was expected that Westerosi
were experienced at battle. But here, this Westerosi king was threatening… tariffs?
Unthinkable! And worse, the other Essosi emissaries were watching. News would spread,
Myr could not afford to be singled out. Any business lost by Myr would clearly be snapped
up by the others.

Everybody clawed for advantage when they could, of course. But it was best to catch a
competitor at a disadvantage without doing anything yourself. They would not be at a
disadvantage!

“We of Myr do thank you for your generosity and cooperation,” the emissary bowed. “You
are most excellent in understanding our concerns and mutual trade relationship, Your Grace.”

He most certainly was not, Rodrik thought. Lord Arryn assured the Myrmen by echoing King

They warned him about the attack on Lannisport. They negotiated such that he had new iron
mines under his power in the Iron Islands. They alerted him to the opportunity to invest in the
Iron Islands Trading Company. And they have befriended Tyrion. And made him… less of a

to make him favorably inclined towards them and to gain good debt from him.
They clearly feared him as well, as was proper, no matter that they would describe such fears
about the consequences of inciting his anger in such blithely vulgar terms. He thought them

“They may play their eccentric little games with the Tyrells,” Tywin finally said. “I certainly
see no reason to warn the Tyrells about those particularly ambitious bannermen of theirs.”

Nobody came to aid him when it came time to put down the Reynes and Tarbecks. Not the
Crown, not anybody. Granted, Tywin would not have tolerated any assistance from outsiders;
it was a challenge that only his House could answer. If you needed help from outsiders
against usurpers, then you were weak. He was not weak. If House Tyrell could not handle
their business, it is simply their weakness and he would waste no time nor money on Reach

“It will be amusing to watch as the years go by,” Gerion quipped.

“You have been invited into their King’s Landing manse?” Tywin asked Tyrion.

“Yes. I will be delivering the clocks that they have ordered and we will be going over some

“I think I shall try to get a deal on glass panels for the clock face covers,” Tyrion went on,

“Well, I want to,” Tyrion said. “The Florents say Casterly Rock’s jewelsmiths are the best, of

Tyrion nodded to himself.

“A fashionable exportable commodity to Essos.”

“And it’s your idea, isn’t it? Not the Florents?” Gerion helpfully asked.

“Yes,” Tyrion smiled with appreciation at his uncle. “Definitely all mine. The Florents are

“Interested enough to get some clocks and then to copy them for their own profit?” Tywin

While Gerion pursed his lips at his older brother, Tyrion shook his head.

“Father, if they did do such a foolish thing, they’d be stealing a Lannister’s idea. Brains

“Well, I think it’s a splendid venture,” Gerion declared. “Show the rest of the court that it’s

“You may begin on establishing a new guild and workshops. After you complete your first

“Thank you, Father,” Tyrion bowed.

The crowd dispersed after the late lunch and everybody made their way back to King’s
Landing. Tyrion was very glad indeed to join up with the Florent party. Uncle Gerion

Tyrion rode in the wheelhouse with Lady Selyse and Lady Samantha. They spent the ride

Tyrion decided to warn Lady Selyse that they have gained the interest of his father. She

“I suppose he would not be so worried if Queen Cersei was any good at diplomacy and truly
cared about working for the greater good of House Lannister.”

Tyrion didn’t hide his confusion; Cersei has always been very proud about being a Lannister.
They all are.

“There are very selfish people in this world,” Selyse said in the tone of a wise woman from a
story. “Who would wreak havoc if only to see to their own desires obtained above all else.
You must be very careful around a person such as her.”

Well, he knew that. She hated him, after all. He didn’t forget how she used to pull his hair or
shoved him, or took his toys from him and held them out of reach over his head, cackling

It only made him think about how not only does Selyse have two fierce protectors in the form

When they arrived at the Foxhole, Tyrion thought that the simplicity and unassuming looks of

of bustling King’s Landing.

The workshop wing of the Foxhole was wondrous. Multiple scholars, discernable by smart

maester gray and wearing their earned links pinned to the breast pockets of the coats, were at

one in Alekyne’s solar, one in Lady Samantha’s chambers, and one in Lord and Lady
Baratheon’s chambers. He’s shipped off another pair of clocks for Erren on Dragonstone and
he’s going to finalize designs for more elaborate clocks for Lord Baratheon’s office in the
Red Keep and one for King Robert.

The Florents favored utility instead of ostentatious ornamentation, so the clocks they
commissioned were in tall polished wood columnar cases, with the hours, minutes, and
second hands all together on one face, unlike his very first clock. The woodworking artisans
of Lannisport were quite aghast at the idea of simplicity (a gift from a son of Lord Lannister
was to showcase their work! Surely Tyrion was joking about preferring the gifts to be
simple!) and the clock cases had scrollwork, fluting, chamfered corners, and little pawed feet.
Secured on the tops of each clock were wooden statues of foxes in different poses depending
on the taste of the particular woodworker to individualize each clock. Selyse was charmed by
one clock that had one fox that seemed to be sleeping, draped languidly over the top of the
clock, its bushy tail curled to frame one side of the clock face. He had a lot of fun
corresponding with Lady Selyse on the matter of designs.

Everybody crowded around the clocks and praised his cleverness. Tyrion felt very proud
indeed and Uncle Gerion had to caution him against getting a puffed up head. He was able to
sit down with Selyse and Stannis to go over the clock that would be in Stannis’ office at the
Red Keep. Stannis agreed that the top of the clock would be surmounted by a carved stag’s
head. A pair of six point antlers from one of Robert’s hunts would be put to use for the
decoration. The pendulum would be carved to seem like an anchor and the trim wood would
be carved to look like rope and sailors knots. And finally, instead of pawed feet, the clock
case would have cloven hooves.

It was Selyse’s idea to start incorporating so called bells and whistles for King Robert’s
clock; why, she even came up with the idea of a little door popping open over the clock face,
with a cunning little bird bowing and flapping its wings on the hour, while two whistles
triggered to echo a cuckoo’s call. Rustic. Charming!

He showed her his in-process sketches; that if one cuckoo was possible, surely there could be
more for the clock to do, no matter that it would quite probably break down more often. She
supposed that another mechanism used for the bobbing of the cuckoo could be reused for the
effect of a leaping stag over the top of the clock. He liked that and wrote down Selyse and
Delena’s suggestions that the clock front could be decorated with properly woodsy motifs
such as carved and painted branches with oak leaves, birds, and squirrels. He already liked
the idea of the clock weights being shaped like pine cones and the pendulum shaped to be
like a maple leaf. Selyse had also joked to him to keep a light touch on any use of gilding for
the clock; Lannisters did like smearing gold all over everything so very much.
This was definitely more fun than his sketches and thoughts on a jake that could be flushed
with water. He would do that in the coming days of his stay. He had originally thought on
getting the manual on how to produce and harness gas from biodigesters, but the layout of the
Rock itself made it impossible. There were no truly quick ways to transport the waste
outdoors; that was why so many tunnels and chutes existed solely for dumping the waste out
into the sea.

Dinner was most convivial. Uncle Gerion was very happy indeed to sit with him and sample
the simpler fare of their table compared to the richly sauced and exotic meats favored by
Casterly Rock. Some of the rumored austerity of Lord Stannis must be an influence. Tyrion

fish with capers and lemon sauce and a braised beef stew made with red wine was a
revelation. Uncle Gerion muttered to Tyrion to make a note to ask for the recipes.

After dinner, they could enjoy the musical stylings of the Florents at large, play table games,
or simply disperse to the various smaller sitting rooms to read. Imry made a furtive

the rules of Mere that he could slip away without notice.

Imry led him alone to a chamber fitted out to be suitable for reading, with padded chairs and
little side tables for holding trays of snacks and drinks. Tyrion took a seat and observed Imry.
He had become restive and almost twitchy, which was very unlike Imry at all.

“This is very odd,” Imry said abruptly. “I’m feeling very nervous. I cannot predict how you
will react, you see.”

“You have a surprise for me,” Tyrion guessed.

“I do.”

“Is it very likely that I won’t like it?” Tyrion tilted his head.

Imry shrugged.

“First of all,” Imry said. “It regards secrets. Lannister secrets.”

Tyrion frowned at that.

“Ah. Is this related to your letters regarding efforts at figuring out the weave of Lord Varys’
webs? Have you found out things you ought not?”

Imry nodded. He leaned forward.

“I found a terrible story regarding you. But rumors being rumors, I set out to find out the

“Terrible rumors are still rumors. Why concern yourself?” Tyrion clasped his hands, starting

of the Florents.
“You are my friend,” Imry immediately replied. “I had to do something.”

“So you’ve done it, I take it,” Tyrion felt like he needed a drink.

Imry nodded.

“I did. I hope- I hope you will like it. Just wait here.”

Imry exited the room. Tyrion sat and waited.

The door opened and the figure of a woman entered. She was dressed in the sober and

“My lord husband.”

“Tysha!”

He gasped for breath, his heart hammering.

“Tyrion?” she held out a hand. “Will you not greet me?”

Tyrion squinched his eyes shut. Tysha said nothing further and the silence stretched.

“I-” and he rubbed at the tears coming from his eyes. “I-”

Tysha stepped closer and drew out a handkerchief and hesitantly held it out to him.

“I don’t know what to say,” Tyrion took the handkerchief. “Tysha.”

“I still love you-”

“I’m sorry-”

They paused, stymied by what they were both about to say. Tyrion took a deep breath.

“I am sorry,” he said. “About the raping. About being such a fool and too useless to stop it.”

Tysha blinked, her own tears forming.

“I still love you,” Tysha said. “T’weren’t your fault. You were always good to me. It was
Lord Lannister who ordered it and I know how it be.”

Tyrion nodded. He wiped at his eyes again and looked at her. How healthy and well she
looked!

“I am glad that you are well,” Tyrion rallied. “And found employment with the Florents at

Tysha dipped her head in agreement.
“But, my lord- Will you not say that you love me too? Or have you forgotten me?”

“I never forgot you!” Tyrion cried, resisting the urge to reach out for her. “I couldn’t! It’s
just-”

“I said I forgave you.”

“I’m not to see you again,” Tyrion recited. “Because you are a whore.”

He looked down, too weak to bear witness to her disappointment and justified anger.

“That was a lie,” Tysha very firmly declared. “‘T’was your own father that did it. There are

Tyrion’s mouth fell open as he looked up at her again. Tysha’s fists clenched as she

“If you will not see me again because I’ve been made a whore, that would be your right, my

They stared at each other until Tyrion jumped down from his chair, reaching to embrace her.

“I’m sorry!” he wept anew. “I’m sorry!”

Tysha nodded, weeping and kneeling to embrace him also. They stayed like that, crying tears

They managed to reaffirm to each other that they still loved each other despite what
happened.

“What’s to become of you?” Tyrion said finally, suddenly afraid.

“Ser Imry says the Florents have ideas.”

Tyrion rushed for the door and opened it. Imry was leaning against the wall opposite. He
raised his eyebrows hopefully upon seeing Tyrion. Tyrion wiped his eyes and smiled, holding
Tysha’s hand.

“Excellent,” Imry clapped his hands once, grinning sharp. “Excellent.”
                 Chapter 39: King's Landing: Step by step


Tyrion and Imry returned to the main hall, to make a show of wanting to retire for the

Imry told Tyrion that they must wait until Uncle Gerion confirmed that he is abed, so Tyrion

Right before Imry turned to take his leave, Tyrion grasped his hand.

“Imry. Imry, my friend. I am deeply, deeply in your debt.”

“I didn’t do it so that I would have a Lannister in my debt,” Imry replied forthrightly.

“Still. I shan’t forget.”

Imry squeezed his hand before letting go and leaving. Tyrion couldn't possibly sleep. It’s all
too amazing. He concentrated on the rising happiness of finding Tysha well, for if he thought
on his father, an equally growing swell of rage threatened to engulf him.

Why?

Oh, he knew, the Florents did not even have to hint in their careful and yet casual way that
Lord Tywin hated his own son. All he had to do was watch the way the Florents acted with
each other and he knew; the difference was too great to not be true. Just because he was a
dwarf.

But there was something else and his mind gnawed on it, gnawed on how it must be his
father who made Jaime lie to him. Forcing Jaime to forswear himself, until he was used to it,
used to chipping away at his own honor until he was a White Cloak and then a Kingslayer,
and kept silent about his reasons because that’s what Father did; twist things, break things,
hurt people. Jaime became a liar because what Father wanted and what Jaime wanted were
almost never the same things, not really, and Jaime doesn’t think!

Maybe, Tyrion thought, he meant to drive Jaime and I apart. Jaime loves me out of our
generation of the Rock. Oh, Aunt Genna is fond, but she’s only able to do so much. And
Uncle Gerion loves me, I think, but nobody cares what he thinks and he knows it; that’s why
he drinks. Uncle Tygett doesn’t even know what to say to me. And forget Uncle Kevan. He’s
like to want Cousin Lancel to be heir to the Rock. It would be the sensible thing to be
ambitious about. Tyrion couldn’t blame him, but it certainly made for a wall between him and
Uncle Kevan.

Father never wants me to have anything good, Tyrion thought. I am to serve and be useful
and out of the way and out of sight, but the minute I am happy, he will interfere.
I don’t know what to do with these facts, Tyrion concluded.

I must wait on Florent thoughts and ideas. They’ll have suggestions and there’s no saying that
I must do as they suggest. They weren’t like Father.

He took off his jacket, shirt and shoes, put on his nightshirt over his trousers and climbed into
bed. When Imry was ready for him, he’ll just slip on his pair of house slippers and his jacket
over his nightshirt. He snuffed out the bedside candle, and laid his head on the pillow. There.
He did hope everybody else goes to sleep at a reasonable time.

His manservant said nothing about Tyrion stuffing his jacket underneath his pillow or the
missing trousers while picking up the rest of the clothes, stoking the fire in the hearth, and
finally, leaving.

He managed to drowse off when a brisk tapping at the door roused him. He was quickly

inside one of the offices within the workshop wing of the Foxhole.

Tysha was there, and Tyrion went to her. Simply sitting next to her, holding her hand, was the
best feeling. Opposite, similarly seated and holding hands, was Lord and Lady Baratheon.
Imry took a seat also.

“I believe Tysha should speak first, as Tyrion must be wanting to know about her last
whereabouts,” Imry suggested.

Tysha nodded and Tyrion prepared himself for the tale. She recounted how she had lain still,
not knowing what else to do in the grip of fear and pain afterwards. She was frightened by
the possibility that any of the Lannister soldiers would come back or the Lord would come
back and finish his punishment upon her by ordering her death. She stayed until she could
hear no sound and only then did she move.

She stacked and rolled the silvers and the gold coin, the greatest amount of money she had
ever seen in her life, into a roll of cloth that she cut from the sheets and tied them about her
waist underneath her dress, gathered up the remaining food, and fled.

She did not wander aimlessly. Luckily the cottage was close enough to The Village By the
Bridge, where her father’s folk came from before he was assigned a new croft by Casterly
Rock’s Head Stewart. She made her way there, hiding in the hedges, ducking out of sight of
all persons; she had already been chased by bandits in the first place and she had thought that
would be the worst of it. She knew better, now.

“So you think you can use your lowborn cunt to catch a lion, do you,” Lord Tywin’s voice
was dire and terrible that day. “A Lannister of the Rock!”

She’d begged. She wept and tried to explain.

She had no idea what was wrong with being with Tyrion, she had thought that if it were
wrong, the septon would have stopped them, or Tyrion would not have asked, or his older
brother, that shining knight Ser Jaime, who was older and must have known such things, he
would have told Tyrion not to.

She had trusted older people to know such things all her young life.

A Lannisport minstrel passing through her father’s village had sung of Jenny of Oldstones
and taught her how to sing Seasons of My Love. A Prince could love a peasant girl and it
made the women at the harvest festival all sigh. Tysha had been enchanted by the thought, as
girls do, and thought it simply was a truth. One was vanishingly unlikely to meet a prince, but
if it weren’t true, they wouldn’t make songs of it, surely?

But she had not understood that whatever was so with one Targaryen prince, was definitely
not so with Tyrion Lannister; his father was Lord Tywin Lannister and the one song about
him told of naught but death and destruction.

So he hurt her and she was not so far gone with terror to not notice how he stared at Tyrion
with that same hateful loathing in his eyes, that same wish to destroy. And Tyrion, poor
Tyrion, gone pale and trembling while his father hissed something low and terrible into his
ear before forcing a gold coin into his hand.

Tysha learned to hate in that moment; banish her, take Tyrion away, even flog her for
reaching so high, and she would be silent and obey, but to do this, to make Tyrion hurt her
last was monstrous.

Tyrion wasn’t the monster rumored by others. It was his father.

Everything ended as abruptly as it started and Tysha had only this thought: Please don’t kill
me after, please don’t kill me, don’t kill me-

She was lucky for that.

She waited by the river, until the local washerwoman arrived one morning to beat and wash
laundry against the rocks, and approached her. She exchanged words, letting it be known that
she was family to locals and asked after any of her father’s kin.

The washerwoman shook her head; the usual sicknesses took their toll and there were none of
her father’s kin alive. However, the washerwoman did believe that she was the daughter of
Denys, son of Walder, son of Rolder. Tysha could not remain with the washerwoman for
long, though the woman was kind enough to invite her to her own dwelling and to have bread
with her. The washerwoman had little enough work to be getting by with; washing the clothes
of unmarried farm laborers who had no womenfolk of their own to do such work.

Tysha gamely tried to let her know of all her skills; she could gut game and fish, she could
mend and sew, cook and clean, she could weave baskets. The washerwoman shook her head,
not wanting to discourage her but needing to, just the same. However, the kind hearted soul
would not have Tysha turned outdoors without a place to lay her head.

It was no trouble at all to get thread and to cut a rod from a tree and to fashion a fish hook
from bone. When the washerwoman washed by the river, Tysha kept her company, fishing. In
exchange for sharing her catches, Tysha could live with her, and sing the pretty songs she
knew in exchange for as long as she needed. Who knows, the washerwoman practically
supposed; perhaps another sickness would come and they’ll be needing extra hands in the
fields for harvesting and threshing.

She lived simply for a time, familiar like her life before with her father, until Ser Imry rode
into the village. She had been sorely afraid once it was known that a stranger was asking after
her, and hid. But Imry was very good at seeming harmless with his mummer’s garb. He sang
to the villagers and even did some odd jobs to help build trust, until he managed to meet her
by the river. He carefully asked about her past until it was clear that she was the one he was
looking for; the girl who was savaged by Lannister soldiers in a cottage near the sea.

He was so soft and careful, speaking low and moving slow and with an expression of such
sympathy that Tysha unburdened herself.

He had very simply asked her if she had it in her heart to see Tyrion ever again; he would
understand if after what Lord Lannister had done, she would not. If she was satisfied with her
lot, she could stay in the village.

She was afraid, of course. But Imry said very clearly that as he was a knight, he would do
what he could to right this wrong, this terrible injustice done against her. She believed him,
yet still feared. She was given the chance to leave Lord Lannister’s land entirely, to go with
him into the Reach, where there was safety within his family’s holdings.

She was no longer an innocent, not after what happened to her. Perhaps he was a liar about
being a Ser as well, and was some kind of procurer, out to spirit young women away and
pressing them into service as whores at some far away brothel. Maybe he was Lord
Lannister’s hired man, after all, like to slit her throat in the night. But she was young, hurt,
and with no prospects in this nameless village. She agreed and rode off with him on his mule.

They journeyed together and Ser Imry proved his word; he was kind to her and certainly did
not attack her in the night. Along the way, he even took out the last proper letter he had
received from Tyrion and read it to her. The turns of phrase and the big words used were so
like Tyrion that she wept at this fleeting presence of her lost husband. She played along with
Ser Imry’s mumming act, quickly learning how to keep a beat on the drum and singing duets

give to her so she could braid them into her hair and tied some bows on her arms to better
match the ribbons on his own sleeves. In this way, they made their way to Brightwater Keep
at last.

Ser Imry apprised his uncle, Lord Florent (how she trembled when she found out that she was
to face yet another lord!) and Lady Florent about her circumstances. They were not cold,
stern, or frightening at all. The Lord merely looked her in the eye and said that he was very
sorry about her misfortunes. The Lady was very kind and took her hand, saying the same.
They got her a chamber of her own in the guest quarters, with such things as a feather bed
and pillows, with fine tapestries on the walls and her own hearth fire!

In the meantime, Ser Imry wrote to his sister, Lady Selyse. The beginnings of a plan were set
to work. They could not let Tyrion know yet. But, she was safe so long as she remained
hidden within Florent holdings.

Tysha was told that Lady Florent would claimher as kin, an Oldflowers.

She would be known as Tysha Oldflowers in Lady Florent’s household, a foster to be
educated amongst young lordlings and ladies. She was shocked by the idea of it, surely such
a lie would be found out! Didn’t the Maesters keep records with their writings and such?

Lady Florent smiled encouragingly and Lord Florent smiled cannily. There were maesters
and then there were maesters. House Oldflowers was not so grand that it was unusual for a
knightly son to strike out on their own in search of service and a living and getting married
far away without informing the main branch until after the fact.

And for that, the last War of the Ninepenny Kings was very useful; so many men had been
sent off and enough never came back. It would be absolutely no trouble at all to claim that
she was a daughter of one of them.

She was afraid that she could not mum her way through this, no matter that she traveled with

others. Lady Florent had firmly informed her that she had no choice. For ill or nil, she was

her to gain her place beside Tyrion should he have her, she would need to be a proper lady.

Tysha thought on the matter for a week and decided that she was afraid of getting caught out,

What worse could happen to her? Death? She was no longer afraid of that.

If, if Tyrion loved her still, then that was enough. It was enough before she knew his place in
the world as a Lannister of the Rock. It would be enough now that she knew better.

She agreed to go along with the Florents with her plan.

So she was bathed, her nails trimmed, her hair brushed and braided, and new clothes made

While the other fosters were are their daily lessons with the Maester, Lady Florent herself
taught Tysha how to read and write. When the other foster girls were at sewing or music

their letters than her, as strange a thought as that was, depending on their Maesters. She
worked especially hard to mimic the noble accent of the Florents.

They were all waiting for a chance to reunite her with Tyrion and to find out what his
response was. The chance finally came and they disguised her yet again in servants’ garb to
hide her in plain sight within the Foxhole, while still maintaining her education. Should he
reject her, her education with the Florents would have made her a bride suitable for another
minor landed knight’s House, no matter that she was no longer a maid. Or, she could continue
to live unmarried with the Florents, finding some suiting occupation from her education.

“I lost you once, I will not again,” Tyrion fiercely declared.

“She is not safe,” Lord Baratheon finally spoke and Tysha shivered at the growl of his voice,
the frown on his face, an echo of Lord Lannister’s menace. “While Lord Tywin lives.”

“Well. There are many easy solutions to that problem,” Imry lightly replied, to Tysha’s gasp.

He noticed Tyrion’s frown.

“Ah, I can’t joke about how your father has it coming to him, as Erren would say?”

“There’s a reason he’s not included in this meeting,” Selyse wryly sighed. “Erren is
excitable.”

“I cannot even begin to consider what ought to be done about Father,” Tyrion shook his head.

“How are you feeling, Tyrion?” Selyse gently asked. “About this? About your father? About
Jaime?”

“Father made Jaime lie to me,” Tyrion grimaced. “I’m sure of it. As for Father?”

He sighed and let go of Tysha’s hand to rub his hand over his moustache.

“He didn’t have to do what he did. It takes nothing but some gold to annul a marriage,
especially as nobody else even knew! Just Jaime and I! I know it now. He did what he did to
be cruel. He treated me, his son, as if I was a Reyne!”

“It is a misfortune when parents hate their children,” Selyse commented.

“I think I always knew. But not- Not truly.”

“Nobody ought to be treated so cruelly as how he treated you two,” Selyse softly said.

Tyrion straightened in his seat. Tysha sniffled and straightened also.

“Imry mentions that you see yourself as in debt to him,” Selyse continued.

“Not just him,” Tyrion formally replied. “I would be honored and pleased as a Lannister to
promise a favor to House Florent should House Florent be in need of a friend in times to
come.”
“Lord Florent will be apprised.”

“I am still not… Not entirely sure why you all have been so generous,” Tyrion said. “Imry
hewing to justice notwithstanding.”

“Trust not in what one says, trust in what one does,” Stannis said. “House Florent plays at
underhanded levity, but they believe in justice. They believe in friendship. They believe in
you. By their efforts, they show their regard.”

Tyrion did not have to think overly long on the matter to agree. His Father was cruel in ways
that preserved the Lannister dominance over the Westerlands. He did not need to turn on his
own son in such a manner. Other disappointed parents could withhold love and regard
without resorting to such measures. It wasn’t fair. But it was true. And Tyrion was done with
his father in that case.

“Well. I’m not a fool like Father thinks. I’ll remember this. A Lannister always pays his debts
and as he’s said enough times, I am a Lannister; I ought to act like one!”

“First decide your goal,” Imry recited. “Then lay out the steps you must take to attain it.”

“Most important of all,” Tyrion looked at Tysha. “I want to Tysha to be safe and well, and for
us to be married, untroubled by others about such a thing.”

“Possible,” Selyse said. “But risky.”

“It must be done most carefully,” Imry added. “If we decide not to do anything about Lord
Tywin.”

“There must always be a Warden of the West,” Stannis pointed out.

“Do you both understand how terribly vital it is that nobody sees the two of you together, that
nobody suspects anything between the two of you?” Selyse addressed Tyrion and Tysha.

They both nodded hastily.

“How shall that be done for me?” Tysha asked. “Am I to go back to Brightwater Keep?”

“Do you wish to? You can be a lady-in-waiting to my mother or even me, if it suit you?”

Tysha considered her choices.

“I would learn more on how to be a Lady of a Great House, if I were to remain with Lady
Florent,” Tysha thought out loud. “But I would learn fancier manners in court.”

“Queen Cersei is here. I would not rest easy in your circumstances being so near that
woman,” Stannis gravely observed.

Tysha looked in question to Tyrion.

“My sweet sister was a most apt pupil of dear Father,” Tyrion snorted.
“Then she is cruel and dangerous,” Tysha realized. “And I cannot avoid her in court because
the Florents go very often.”

“Are you prepared to be separated in this manner, with Tyrion at Casterly Rock and you at
Brightwater Keep?”

“We must,” Tysha firmly said. “To keep both of us safe. ‘Tis as Tyrion says; his own lord
father treated him like a Reyne and everybody knows what happened with them. I’ll not be
cause for putting him in danger.”

“You will still be able to write letters, of course,” Imry said. “Though Tysha ought to direct
the letters to the Foxhole and then we arrange for dead drops that Tyrion can reach.”

That made sense to Tyrion.

They worked out a plan to be expanded over time. Selyse reminded the both of them that they
were both still young; she herself was not married until twenty-one. Tysha would need all the
time possible for polishing and occasional appearances at court, to be seen with the Florents
when Lord Florent had cause to visit King’s Landing. It was impossible that a peasant should
be married to a Lannister. But a minor noble? Even from as small a House as Oldflowers?
Not too impossible. Especially since Lord Tywin’s own sister was married to a Frey.
Oldflowers could boast Gardener blood.

Tyrion himself needed to gain a bloc of support for himself within Casterly Rock. He had to
expect that Lord Tywin would suffer it to go to one of his nephews. Working from this
assumption, Tyrion had to maneuver himself in such a way that he would be allowed leeway
from a notoriously controlling Lord Paramount, let alone a father. Selyse and Imry laid out
the beginnings of a campaign to give his reputation and presence much needed luster.

It was true that as a dwarf, the traditional lordly pursuits (besides his early bouts of whoring
and drinking after being punished for Tysha) were not going to be attainable.

Height had nothing to do with hawking, Stannis suggested. Here, he had more than enough
expertise on the handling of raptors and would be willing to be seen escorting Tyrion through
the King’s Wood for the purpose, with a party of suitably gossipy lords on sevendays when
Tyrion had cause (and he would have plenty) to visit King’s Landing. Stannis and Lord Hand
Arryn had agreed with Robert that as he was doing his duties so much more often that he
ought to have one hunt a moon to relax. Robert was very enthusiastic about spending time
with both of his brothers and Stannis found the benefits of what Selyse termed schmoozing in
a setting less imposing than the Red Keep.

There was also the fact that the hunts, being so much more rare than rounds of Hammerball
or soccer, were very exclusive. Robert himself saw the sense in a properly small hunting
party that would not slow him down nor scare away the game for miles. The Florents were
very happy to use the hunting parties as a way to test out war campaign gear. As far as Selyse
was concerned, there was nothing that could not be made to fold out of a large trunk or
otherwise made to quickly dismantle and stowed away. A camp bed with a padded mattress.
A dispatch writing desk with compartments for papers and writing instruments. Washstands.
A larger table with legs that unscrewed and then the table top folded in half and became a
box case that held the legs within. A brass candle lantern that folded flat into a rectangle.

Imry suggested that Tyrion may even be interested in the ongoing project of Alekyne’s to
improve bows and crossbows with cams. That would give him an excuse to visit the Foxhole
more often and eventually allow him to be seen having some weapons handling ability to
show for it.

Tyrion supposed that would be beneficial to show the gossipmongers at court that he was
capable in a way.

Selyse had heard from her mother, who heard from her gossipy sewing circles that included
Crownlander and Westermen women that instead of a drunken, lustful monster, after his
showing at the last feast, where he ably danced the foxtrot and did not over imbibe wine that
he was starting to seem respectable.

He would need to concentrate on building up the business of his clockmaking endeavor,
increasing volume and quality as he went, starting first at Lannisport and with the aim to set
up shops in King’s Landing. And with that, of course he would need to supervise at King’s
Landing. While there, he should get himself a manse in his name, with his own funds.

While at King’s Landing, he would be seen with Alekyne and Renly; respectable heirs better
known for being bookish and favoring indoor games and artistic pursuits when they weren’t
engaged in suitably martial activities. Even better, Renly was to be a Lord Paramount. It
would even be an echo of Lord Tywin and Lord Steffon’s friendship. They would see to
gaining inroads with the Westerland bannermen Houses who had presence at King’s Landing.
It is here that they had to move most carefully; Cersei would be very dangerous indeed once
it became clear to her that Tyrion would be issuing his own dinner and lunch invitations and
afternoon amusements.

It would be no trouble at all to have Lady Lysa issue him an invitation to the smaller dinners
within Lord Hand Arryn’s chambers. Immediate inclusion in this very exclusive list of
approved guests would do much for his reputation. There was also the fact that if he was the
only Lannister who mattered with access to the Lord Hand, his father simply must take him
into consideration.

Tyrion asked if Uncle Gerion could be included somehow in all this scheming. Of course, he
would not know about Tysha. The matter was thought on and Imry suggested that as Tyrion
would now be seen making regular trips to King’s Landing that perhaps his uncle could be
convinced to be a part of his retinue, as it was known that Gerion was often at cross purposes
with his oldest brother.

Tyrion thought it would not be too difficult to accomplish.

He would miss Tysha dearly, but having work and amassing funds that he would not have to
account for with his father suited him.

Tysha would continue her education and make visits to the Foxhole, where general exposure
would allow her chances to perhaps contribute and increase her own funds. She was already
working as hard as possible to learn Reacher noble manners.

They would go on with their separation until Tyrion had enough independence and support
from other nobles such that if he were to marry her publicly, they could stand as witnesses
and he would be too valuable, too well known for Lord Tywin to make reprisal; he would risk
losing too much in goodwill.

Satisfied and all of them yawning, they left to each of their own quarters. Imry kindly let
Tyrion and Tysha have a moment alone together; for they surely could not be seen by even
the Florent servants.

They embraced and kissed.

“I miss you already,” he sniffed. “But it will all be worth it, Tysha.”

“I know. You shall make everything well,” Tysha squeezed him tightly. “And when you next
visit the Foxhole, I shall have some embroidered handkerchiefs for you, by my hand. I’m
learning embroidery, you see.”

“I look forward to reading your letters,” Tyrion stepped back.

Tysha nodded, kissed him again, and they separated down the halls.
              Chapter 40: King's Landing: Bear with Me


Tyrion and his retinue stayed on in King’s Landing after the Ironmen lords took their leave,
backtracking to Seaguard escorted by the Florent men-at-arms assigned by Imry. It was
during this time that it was announced that Lord Alester Florent and Lord Jorah Mormont
came to an accord and that Alekyne Florent and Dacey Mormont were officially betrothed.

The disparity in means and the lack of prior importance of the Mormonts in the doings of the
royal court set tongues wagging. Most spurious was the rumor that Alekyne was caught in
Dacey’s bed and that Jorah demanded satisfaction on the matter of her honor. Some supposed
that the lady in question was comely enough and that there was no reason it could not be a
love match. Others claimed that the Mormonts held to some mysterious Northern custom,
whereupon if a woman could best a man at arms, the man could be taken as spoils for a
husband.

It was certainly true that Dacey was seen routing Alekyne in the Red Keep’s training yard
with rapid blows of her mace and a well-timed leg sweep. Bawdy jokes were made of the
foolhardy fox making to mount such a fierce bear.

More was noted about how simply unfortunate it must be for Lord Alester to have made such
prestigious matches for the womenfolk of his family and for his heir to let him down by
choosing a lady of such a poor, out of the way House. Plenty watched, trying to discern any
break in paternal regard from Lord Alester. Those who encountered him at any number of
dinners and entertainments or court appearances could conclude nothing; Lord Alester
showed naught but that infuriating, knowing, smirking smile that hinted at anything and
nothing. Alekyne would only say that he was pleased by his betrothed, ignoring the more
pointed questions posed by the other Reacher lordlings and knights at court.

Dacey would be staying on as a guest of the Manderly’s in their King’s Landing manse for
propriety’s sake. Out of all the Northern Houses the Manderlys had most cause to maintain a
presence at King’s Landing, where one or another cousin or trusted servant could keep
abreast of Small Council doings, make note of trends in trade, and receive instructions
regarding any potential House petitions of import great enough to require the attention of the
King instead of Lord Stark, rare as those were.

Dacey Mormont had never been to King’s Landing before. Nobody could recall a Mormont
besides Lord Jorah venturing South, though surely his father and other Bear Islanders served
during the War of the Ninepenny Kings. It was judged that of course perhaps the men sent
over was so small a contingent that they were simply forgotten. Forgettable.

When the announcements regarding the Ship Launch reached Bear Island, Jorah was not
planning to make a showing, not until a raven message followed from Lord Stark. Lord Stark
was in correspondence with King Robert and Robert was so excited about the endeavors of
his good-kin and Lord Stark was prudently curious about the results of his House’s
investment in the Iron Island Trading Company. He requested that the Mormonts, along with
House Glover, Ryswell, Dustin, and Flint’s Finger Flints, as Houses with experience dealing
with Ironmen, to be present, to give him a true report on how the lords seemed. The House
Manderly would also be present for the purpose, as they were by the far the most experienced
in the North with ships.

Jorah supposed that no other Northern Houses would be interested despite Lord Stark’s
interest being so great that he managed to have his brother Benjen present.

Jorah and his cousin Dacey traveled to Winterfell to discuss in greater detail with Lord Stark
what he wished to know. He greeted Master Galbert Glover with careful cordiality; their
mutual grieving over the death of his late wife Agnes Glover, Galbert’s sister, had put pause
to correspondence. They clasped hands and discussed quickly and Jorah found that both of
them were carefully curious about the whole matter; they had no love for Ironmen, no, but
the idea of an enterprise that would rival the Arsenal of Braavos was surely something new
and worth consideration. The quarrelsome Lord Rodrik Ryswell was present and Jorah
avoided him for his complaining about the upcoming traveling southward. He was dutiful, oh
yes, he proclaimed, but the roads were dusty, the food at inns gave him the wind, and on and
on and on. Jorah thought he would prefer the company of an Umber instead of a Ryswell, no
matter that Umbers seemed to permanently bellow instead of using regular speech. Lady
Dustin sent nobody. Lord Iver Flint showed himself, with a skeptical cant to his brow, but
thankfully not prone to complaints, not like Lord Ryswell.

Ser Wylis Manderly represented his House and had much useful information. He brought
with him reports and rumors regarding King’s Landing’s court and the state of trade. His own
wife, being a Woolfield, told him of the excitement from her House about Southron wool
merchants regarding the bulk pricing they could get from wool. Already, good wool fabrics
were filtering into White Harbor and the improved quality, as well as being cheaper than
handspun and handwoven cloth, was causing an upheaval of business practices. These fabrics
were Reacher stuffs, coming out of the mysterious mills and factories held by the Florents
and Tarlys (of all Houses). There were rumors that the same kinds of mills and factories were
present in Storm’s End holdings, which was unsurprising as it was known that Lord Renly
was fostered with the younger Florents.

Lord Stark saw the sense of making contact with the Florents on the matter. Perhaps the
Florents would be loathe to release the secrets of their clothmaking to the North. Or more
likely, they would wish to draw up contracts allowing for some sort of partnership or leasing
agreements. Either way, Ned was keen to see more Northmen clothed warmly with coppers
per yard of wool. Benjen was privately advised to receive the Florents, to not take offense by
their impertinent ways, and to try not to panic should any very shocking statements be made.
Benjen raised an eyebrow at this, until Ned made a significant look at Jon Snow, now known
as Benjen’s bastard. On this secret matter, Benjen readily followed, once Ned explained it all,
and extended affection to his hidden nephew openly when he made trips to Winterfell.

Ser Wylis was wise enough to bring a bolt of Reacher wool to show the lords assembled and
Jorah and Dacey were impressed by the uniformity of the weave, to say nothing of the price.
If they could get it for even cheaper should Lord Stark convince the Florents to release looms
somehow to anyone in the North, what a great boon that would be!
After meeting and planning, everyone and Benjen went with Wylis southward to White
Harbor where they would sail on to King’s Landing. While being feasted there by the
Manderlys, Jorah and Dacey were shown a printed book from Bellflower Press regarding
current court etiquette and how to dance the Foxtrot by the Manderly sisters. House Florent’s
influence on the Master of Ships and the Royal Fleet was known; not only for the
provisioning contract with the Crown, but the Manderlys could point out the Royal Fleet
ships with regular patrol routes between White Harbor and King’s Landing, with their
gleaming brass hulls, bristling armaments, and flying daring amounts of sail. The captains
readily told all who asked that Florent ideas caused these engineering changes.

Dacey was told by Wylla and Wynafryd that as all the Florent men were as yet unmarried, not
even betrothed, that their grandfather wished to see about catching one of them for
themselves. They spoke readily of both trying seriously to catch the eye of the heir, Alekyne.
Rumors had it that Reacher as he was, he was not a typical soft Southron lordling, known
only for carousing and entering into tournaments. He favored the bow and arrow for both
hunting and on the battlefield, had a good seat while riding, and most interesting of all, was
blessed with a beautiful singing voice. He was said to bathe at least once a week, had all his
teeth, and was a good dancer.

Dacey was cautiously interested in what she heard. She asked Jorah for what he remembered
of any of the Florents during the Greyjoy Rebellion. He said that as they were all on an
entirely different island than him, he could say nothing about their showing on the battlefield.
However, both the younger Florent cousins were knighted by their uncle Ser Colin
afterwards. Lord Stark seemed predisposed to like the Florents. And it was said that all the
Florents were friends, strange seeming as it was, with the famously prickly Lord Stannis
Baratheon. In order to befriend the likes of the Master of Ships, they had to be dutiful and
honorable men, at the least. During the feast at Lannisport, they danced and were all very
good at the task. He had not seen any untoward behavior towards any women; not ladies nor
serving girls. He had not heard any rumors of other vices either, but he himself was not prone
towards gossip of that sort anyway.

Jorah then made a knowing look at Dacey and asked if she was entering the lists in the
tournament of charms all the young ladies seemed to be entering for a Florent’s favor. Dacey
replied that she might as well; she may not suit some soft Southron lordling, but she was as
good as any lady from any other lordly House for marrying, just as a single Bear Island
warrior was worth ten men from anywhere else in the whole world in a fight. Jorah chuckled
and agreed it was so and they practiced the foxtrot together, so that she could truly show
herself to best advantage. Dacey kindly jested to Jorah that perhaps in all the feasting and
fuss about the Ship Launch that he might find a second wife. Jorah shrugged. He supposed
there may be looks askance at his lady cousin being heir unless she chose to marry off of the
Island, but Bear Islanders cared little for the opinions of outsiders.

When they arrived at King’s Landing, fellow veterans of the Greyjoy Rebellion greeted Jorah
warmly, so that they at least did not have complete strangers beside them within the Great
Hall, to see the Ironmen. While they waited, Jorah pointed out the Florents, gathered by the
Iron Throne’s dias, standing with Lord Baratheon. They were a tall family, and though the
women hid the characteristic ears with the way they arranged their hair, it was easy to see it
of the men. Only Lord Florent kept his greying hair long to his shoulders, brushed to cover
his ears, looking very distinguished indeed with his pointed beard. They formed a striking
cluster of blue-clad figures, with flashes of orange at their collars and wrists.

The one who was Alekyne shared the lean, angular face of his father, kept clean shaven, and
his sandy-colored forelocks parted on one side and brushed away from his face. He was in
conversation with his cousins. As brothers, there was obvious resemblance between Ser Imry
and Ser Erren. Both had stronger noses, shared by their sister, Lady Baratheon. Ser Imry was
tanned, had a moustache, wore his hair like Alekyne, and Dacey noticed that he chose to wear
a dagger at his hip and one in a boot, in addition to a sword. His brother in contrast was pale,
with his hair closely cropped short. He was not overly armed like his brother, preferring to
simply wear a sword.

All of the Florents had restless eyes, scanning the crowd as if they were on guard, though
they held conversation and greeted those that went up to them with gracious attentiveness.
Each of them made eye contact with her and each of their gazes slid away just as quickly,
with no change in their studiously pleasant expressions. Jorah noted that to smile too quickly
upon catching any lady’s eye in a gossipy court was unwise.

Jorah maneuvered the both of them through the crowd after the Florents finished greeting the
Ironmen and they succeeded in greeting Lord Florent in good time. Lord Florent proceeded
to introduce his kin and Alekyne stepped forward first to greet Dacey as she curtsied.

Alekyne took her hand and bowed over it, pressing a polite kiss to the back of her hand.

When he stood back up, he tilted his head, a light of curiosity in his eyes.

“Calloused hands, my lady?”

Dacey barely resisted quickly drawing her hand back behind her back from him noticing.

“My cousin favors the mace,” Jorah said proudly. “She has no small skill with it.”

Dacey lifted her chin, daring any of these Southron lords to look askance. Instead, Alekyne

“Interesting. Do you spar with men?”

“The Ironmen who attack Bear Island are men,” Dacey replied. “So of course I do.”

“Then will you spar with me, these coming days?”

“And me!” Ser Erren’s head popped out from behind Alekyne’s shoulder. “We’ve not had

Ser Imry looked fondly exasperated at his brother interrupting, but he looked at her with that

Dacey nodded. Perhaps they meant to mock her in the yard, but she’ll show all of them.
Alekyne asked of their journey down south with genuine curiosity, wanting to know what

Dacey found that she approved of this sort of attitude. The Manderly sisters were very

It was one thing to dance with as familiar a family member as her Cousin Jorah or a jolly,

Benjen Stark was expected to leave the first, as he continues to have Night’s Watch duties. It

After Alekyne, young Lord Renly asked her for a dance. After that, one after another of the
