On that subject, the Manderly sisters were most useful, flitting about from one group of

Dacey was not so sure; Ser Imry was worldly and traveled and he certainly had a dashing air

The next day, they made their way to the Wendwater Royal Shipyard and the ship was lovely.
Bear Islanders had their own fishing skiffs, of course, and they were familiar with the trading
ships that enter their harbor, but such craft were all nothing to the sheer size and beauty of the

explain.

Some men very rudely started asking her questions for the purpose of tripping her up, but she
proved equal to their questions. Too many did not believe that most of the engineering and
design was spearheaded by the lady in question, supported by the teams of engineers hired on
from Oldtown by the Florents. Dacey was further gratified by how Alekyne and the Florent
men readily deferred to Lady Rhea for the more technical questions, freely giving her credit.

The launch was simply wonderful. During the lunch after, a number of the Florent ladies
went with Lady Arryn to speak to the Gulltown Arryns. Jorah understood Dacey’s purpose
enough and quietly went to the periphery of the group of young lords gathered around

Instead of attempting to join any number of young ladies who were sitting in groups away

motherhood, with a darling round-faced young son who bowed very correctly and a number

some delicate Southron way of going about it, but she was but a Bear Island woman, so she
asked very frankly about what his older sister had to say about Alekyne.

Lady Melessa was unstinting about her praise. By the time he was sixteen, he was already
approaching their father about improvements to Brightwater Keep and its holdings, already
shadowing their steward and asking their Uncle Axell questions when he was auditing their
household accounts, already sitting in on petition sessions and comfortable riding out to meet
with their smallfolk and resolving issues. Lady Melessa added with a twinkle in her eye that
Dacey was very welcome to attend the musicales that they were in the habit of holding at the
Red Keep for the entertainment of the King.

Lady Melessa freely told Dacey about Alekyne’s hopes for a wife; that he wanted somebody
sensible and thrifty first off, with hopes that felicity in marriage would come from a
compatibility in sensibility and that the woman in question could share in laughter, as the
Florents loved to laugh and play as much as they valued duty and occupying their days with
work.

Dacey thanked her for her frankness with her and took her leave. She would need to ask
Cousin Jorah later what he thought of Alekyne and how he comported himself when amongst
men. She returned to the Manderly sisters. Both were a little disappointed that Alekyne took
no notice of them, but they said that they were told by other ladies that regularly attended
court that none of the Florent men made any distinctions in general. They were favorite
guests at dinners, ready with anecdotes and amusing stories, could appreciate efforts at
singing or on the harps or bells, and were not impatient when shown embroidery work. The
puzzle was that Alekyne would ask young ladies about matters that they were sure would be
better answered by asking their fathers or brothers; about managing holdings, about livestock
and harvests, about the health of their smallfolk. When he wasn’t doing that, he was asking
confusing questions about what they thought some old piece of historical event or occurrence
meant, as if they ever aspired to be maesters!

Bear Island was small and insular enough that Dacey could not have afforded to not know the
smallfolk. What an idea! They had to be very careful indeed to put by for winters, to know
who was ill and not, to carefully stock up on medicinal herbs, to keep watch on the coasts for
pirates and to be ready to repel reavers. There were also the bears on Bear Island, of course.
Should a bear decide to invade a crofter’s pigpen to make off with a hog, everybody had to
quickly work together; children had to be carried off to safety, and men set to keep watch to
see that it left in an orderly manner and for the crofter in question to be compensated. Hounds
would be gathered, their baying encouraged to drive off the bear, and everybody would be on
alert for days, until it was clear that the bear moved on back to the interior of the island.

Dacey supposed she was not so learned a person as the Florents, but it seemed that it was as
true as Lady Melessa claimed; he was not looking for a pretty flower to display in his hall, to
merely preside over entertainments. He wanted a capable woman, who knew to maintain a
keep in good order. Dacey was sure she could do that, at least. If there was a House that can
make do with little, it was House Mormont. If he or his father had not chosen any of these
soft Southron ladies for a bride by now, then truly, she was not being blindly optimistic about
her chances.

The day after that, Jorah and Dacey followed a Red Keep servant to the training yard. The
King himself was there, happily bellowing as he sparred with two White Cloaks at the same
time. They moved on to another part of the large yard, until they found the Florents. They
were wearing short-sleeved shirts and worn out loose short trousers, suitable for training
sessions. They were standing in front of a structure that Dacey had never seen before. There
were bars that looked like chin up bars and Dacey would have thought they were for the
purpose, except the structures were notched and taller than necessary and built over bales of
straw covered with canvas.
“Ah, good morn!” Ser Erren called out. “You’re just in time to see the race!”

“Most chin ups in a minute?” guessed Jorah.

“To the top first!” Ser Imry pointed up to the topmost of the structure. The structure had long
ropes tied to it, adjacent to the notched parts.

“We will spar afterwards, if it suit, Lady Dacey?” Alekyne waved at her.

“I look forward to it,” Dacey replied, smiling.

It was not exactly clear how they would ascend, unless it was by shimmying up the ropes.
Jorah and Dacey moved away, to get a clearer view. The three Florents arranged themselves
into position and at a whistle from one of the men-at-arms, all of them took running jumps to
clear the straw bales and caught hold of the chin up bars.

A heaving flex of their arms and Dacey gasped as the men made the bars jump from the
notches and hook into position on a higher set of notches.

“Ingenious,” Jorah murmured.

“They call it the salmon ladder,” Benjen Stark mentioned after he made his way to stand

interesting.”

Cheers and yells came from the group of bystanders as the Florents made their way. Ser Imry

dangled unbalanced. He adjusted for it with another jump, but that was enough for Ser Erren
to get ahead. In the end Ser Imry finished first at ten jumps and he shimmied back down
using the rope. Ser Erren finished second and Alekyne third.

His cousins did not harry him too much for losing; they all said it was clearly because he was

to cause an imbalance. Jorah himself tried and succeeded in jumping four rungs, before the

more than typical obstacle course, one that had the men climbing, jumping, and balancing as
they went. Jorah was glad to have found something to interest him given their tentative plans
for staying in King’s Landing. Omer and Merrell approached and said that there was a setup
at the Florent manse, the Foxhole, suitable for a woman to try, as the notches were placed
closer together to accommodate them when they were younger. At this time of day, it would
be Samwell Tarly training. They were here because their cousin Sam would rather practice
out of sight by himself. He was a little shy.

In the time that Dacey spoke to them, while the older Florents left to get into their armor, it
was clear that they did not find her an oddity to be mocked. They were all merely extremely
curious.
Dacey was impatient to fight Alekyne, to see if he was the sort to hold back when faced with
a woman or somebody who would be serious about testing skill. From the first blocked strike

Jorah’s hits. She exhaled and lunged with her shield to bash him and he danced backwards.
They circled, trading hits, until she was sure. He had greater reach than Cousin Jorah, but
reach was nothing once she closed.

The opportunity came and she bellowed, charging, her sparring mace clanking with rapid
strikes at his shoulders and helmet, until she tripped him with a practiced move and he fell
with a great crash of armor. She brought her mace down with a decisive blow to the dirt
beside his head; obviously she had the killing strike.

“I yield!”

Alekyne lifted the visor of his helmet, laughing.

“Marvelous!” he cried out.

The Florents were clapping for her, fair as they were. King Robert himself was there,
clapping a congratulatory hand on Cousin Jorah’s back, laughing about how he had missed
being around a Northern woman of spirit.

Dacey held out her hand and Alekyne did not hesitate to take it in order to get up.

There was clapping from above and Dacey raised her head to see ladies observing from the
overhead gallery. Lady Baratheon and her lady cousins waved. Dacey waved back.

After that, it was Ser Erren, who was most eager. They traded blows until she had the
measure of his reaction time and she was able to stun him with the edge of her shield while
smacking him soundly with her mace. Ser Imry was the one to finally win; she was beginning
to get winded and he favored an arming sword and dagger. As evidenced by him winning at
the salmon ladder, he had tremendous force behind his double-handed strikes and he was the
fastest amongst his kin.

Dacey had more opportunity to speak with Alekyne as they rested between bouts, where
Cousin Jorah usefully gave them the time to do so by agreeing to spar with the Florents and
the King. He inquired about her training, about her other interests, about what she would
most desire in the future. She replied that she liked hunting and the feeling of peace that came
from wandering into a deep forest. On the subject of the future, she was not so sure that she
could reveal her thoughts on so short an acquaintance.

Alekyne smiled and invited her to join a hunting party in the Kingswood if she would like.

“I wish to be better acquainted, don’t you?” he asked.

She was curious. And if she was honest with herself, his strength at arms and the strength in
his arms was compelling.

“I wish it also,” she replied. “Your sister mentioned a musicale, tonight?”
“Yes. Will I see you there?”

Dacey nodded.

King Robert never did forget how fine the Florents sounded in Storm’s End and found that he
quite enjoyed having some entertainment from his good-kin, for as many imitators there were
amongst the court musicians, they didn’t have the same quality. Not the swagger, as Erren
would say. So every so often (but especially on this occasion with the Ship Launch, allowing
for more of the Florents to be present) the Florents put on private shows for the court’s
amusement.

There was no particular protocol of dress needed and it was informal enough compared to a
ball or feast that children were often in attendance. The food was also kept simple, being
soups and bread bundles. As it was an idea of the Florents, and with all of them present, this
latest one turned into a showcase for their talent; usually there were slots and ladies (or men)
who wished to perform would sign up. Not many did; why would they, when they could hire
mummers? There were not half so many who wished to attend the musicale as for a proper
feast or ball and far more women than men at that. When Dacey and Jorah entered the
smaller hall set aside for the occasion, they were waved down by an eager Wylla to take a
seat; the sisters were unfashionably early and took over the seats for them in anticipation.

Dacey could appreciate any musical talent at all; with so few mummers making the trip to
Bear Island, anybody who can hold a tune or even whistle creditably were popular in the
evening gatherings at home.

As guest, House Caron’s own Lord Bryce was first up and he sang very well indeed, a ballad
in the robust and simple style of the Stormlands. King Robert smiled and clapped. It really
was a pity, Dacey thought to herself, that no other of his family were present; it was said that
Caron voices were famously sweet and to hear a Caron lady was to hear rare talent.

Next up were the youngest Florents, Omer and Merrell with Lord Renly. Samwell Tarly stood
up also with the accompanying musicians, surprisingly, clutching a tambourine and looking
unsure. The musicians began and the three singers arranged themselves into a line and started
stepping and rocking in unison. They sang an older Florent favorite, ‘I Can’t Help Myself’.
Sam was blushing, but he was definitely keeping up on his tambourine, buoyed by the
clapping along of his mother Melessa in the audience. His father grumbled to himself, but
had to behave as Melessa’s elbow was unerring and sharp and he was sitting beside Lord
Florent.

At the end of the song, the cousins and Lord Renly clapped for Sam, who flushed brighter
while grinning, as this was his first performance in front of a proper gathering. Dacey
clapped, charmed and quite liking the happiness of the song. Lady Delena went up alone, to
perform ‘Girl from Ipanema’. Dacey frowned curiously, having never heard of such a place
before, but the idea of it, the quiet lovelorn quality of the song was wonderful. She had never
heard a song its like. Lady Delena’s smoky, evocative voice was in good form for her next
song, ‘Here Comes the Rain Again’, to more applause. Lady Delena made her bow.

The original three of Ladies Selyse, Melessa, and Rhea stood up and performed ‘Be My
Baby’, and Dacey smiled to see Imry joining the backing musicians, with a pair of spoons
clinking away in rhythm. They went through older favorites: ‘Cherry Pink and Apple
Blossom White’, ‘How Deep is Your Love’ and ‘You Can’t Hurry Love’. Dacey found it
charming, how they stepped and swayed like the younger Florents while coquetting with their
shoulders and making little elegant gestures of their hands and saucy smiles.

And lastly, Selyse stood alone, announced that she dedicated a song to her husband, Lord
Stannis. Dacey looked, along with everybody else, at Lord Stannis, who sat beside the King.
He blinked and the King laughed and clapped him on the shoulder. Violins softly started and
her powerful voice rang out with the first notes of ‘At Last’. Dacey was moved to press her
hands to her cheeks, transported by the way Lady Selyse sang to Lord Stannis, gesturing
towards him with her hand and the way he blinked at her, a little awestruck, a little
embarrassed, and returning her bright smile with a brief, small smile of his own.

In the end, it was Alekyne, Imry, Erren, and Omer on the stage. They arranged themselves
and began some slower songs: ‘Put Your Head on My Shoulder’, ‘Only the Lonely’, ‘The
Best is Yet to Come’, ‘Two Occasions’, and ‘Unchained Melody’. Alekyne took turns with

with his delivery that was enchanting. Dacey put a hand to her mouth, as she could not help
smiling at Alekyne as he stepped and strut through his songs, culminating with the apparent
crowd favorite of ‘Can’t Take My Eyes Off of You’.

She and Cousin Jorah stood to applaud the Florents, who grinned and waved. It was late and
they had to go. Dacey pulled on Jorah’s hand and they stayed behind a little longer. A number

giggling, cooing well-wishers. Alekyne and his cousins were all gracious, bowing again and

Alekyne and she smiled. He smiled back, she was sure of it. She would elbow her way
through the crowd to him, but surely that was too uncouth here in the South.

They met again in the mornings at the training yard before a party of Florent family went out
into the Kingswood for a hunt. There were plenty of moments for the two of them to
converse and Dacey found herself charmed. She felt that he was just as a young lord ought to
be; sensible, yet lively, dutiful, yet with happy manners. As she was a Bear Island woman,
she directly informed him within a fortnight of their stay in King’s Landing that should he go
to his father to inform him to begin marriage negotiations, she would not be opposed.
Alekyne laughed cheerfully and said that though she claimed she was not opposed, it was not
such an encouragement as she thought. Did she truly consider their chances of marital
felicity?

Dacey pursed her lips, which made him smile, wondering on how forward she could afford to
be in the South.

“I think you would make a good a husband as I could hope,” Dacey said. “I do not know the
fancy words you do or how to make them go so poetically. But I surely know that I like you.”

“Like?” Alekyne tilted his head, with a reassuring seriousness in his look.

“More than any man I’ve met. Enough to stake my life with yours. Now you know.”
“I like you, also. Definitely. Tremendously. Outrageously.”

Dacey laughed as Alekyne went on.

“Then you had better go and tell your father. I will speak with Cousin Jorah.”

“Expeditiously!” he grinned, and left to ride immediately to the Foxhole.

Lord Alester was not overjoyed at the prospect of a bride for his heir who would bring
nothing except timber and a few bearskin rugs as dowry, if that. Bear Island was that poor.
However, he had long been used to the ways the young Florents could lay out their arguments
to get their way and his son was silver-tongued, at that. Alekyne saw that Dacey got on with
his sisters and Cousin Selyse; surely between the three of them had they found any serious
fault they would have informed him. That was in addition to his own quietly building
network of informants. She was of irreproachable reputation and only scandalous in the
South because she used a weapon in the traditional manner of her people. He certainly didn’t
disapprove and in fact was more enamoured with her because of it. What warriors their
children could be!

She was earnest and plain-spoken. This might have been boring compared to the sophisticates
of court, but there was a sheer honesty and practicality in her manner also echoed by Lord
Jorah that Alekyne was starting to see was a prototypical Northern way, after conversing with
Benjen Stark, and the lords Flint, Glover, and Ryswell. She knew her people, she knew Bear
Island, there was so much that she knew firsthand about being a good sort of noble; the kind
that took fealty and duty to smallfolk seriously. Perhaps she didn’t know the words and
concepts about the inherent dignity of the common people as posited and championed by
Selyse in their private evening talks at the Foxhole, but she lived it. On so small and
precarious an island holding, the Mormonts held fast and lived true and free without needing
to resort to reaving the Iron Islands way. There were thousands of years worth of toughness
bred into the Mormont line, no matter that there were rumors of the shaky paternity of any of
the Mormont lords given the propensity of the women for having “missing husbands”. He
was Florent. His House needed a tough woman. He found one such. For all that he himself
enjoyed wordplay and subterfuge, it would be a relief to have no such pretenses in the safety
of home. To have something of that honesty he observed between Selyse and her Stannis. Of
course it didn’t hurt that Dacey was also attractive to look upon.

Between Alekyne’s reasoning and sentiments and Selyse’s confirmation that this would be a
suitable social misdirection for the gossiping courtiers of King’s Landing in service to their
House’s myriad workings, he went to meet with Lord Jorah. Lord Alester could afford to be
generous. The current accountants of Brightwater Keep were very well trained by Axell, and
it was no trouble at all to have a summary report on the incomes and net profits of the various
Florent business holdings brought together. Jorah’s eyebrows raised once it became clear that
his niece would be provided for beyond his wildest ambitions.

“Whatever is the traditional amount a Mormont lady brings with her in marriage, we
appreciate and accept. But as my son has no want for funds or material things, let us speak on
how my House can benefit yours, shall we?”
The gifts to the Dragonstone smallfolk, to Lord Harlaw, to the Royces, would pale beside the
bounty that Lord Alester would vest upon House Mormont and Bear Island. To begin with
Lord Jorah was given the opportunity to build Mormont Keep anew, not with costly imported
stone, but with an engineered building substance of the Florents, called concrete. Planning for
a network of signal towers. The fighting men and women of Bear Island would be given new
forged armor and weapons, the crofters would have the seed drills, harvesters, threshers, and
new waterwheels or windmills to power mills, the fishermen would have new fishing nets,
and yards and yards of good cloth; canvas for sails and tents for hunters, cotton and wool for
clothing. He would gain an entire new library of useful and entertaining books. The works of
the Florents were many and they would have them at Bear Island from the love of the Florent
heir.

Jorah accepted readily. He knew that the Florents could not be so generous for no reason;
surely they had interests in the North and wanted his House as an intermediary with Lord
Stark. That can only benefit House Mormont. His only real stipulation was that Dacey be
married in a godswood, in front of a proper heart tree. Alester agreed to that easily;
Brightwater Keep had a small godswood of its own, with a heart tree that had a quizzical
face. In the meantime, they could plan for the wedding and the Mormonts could begin the
improvements immediately to Bear Island. A small celebratory dinner was held in the
Foxhole and Dacey and Jorah were gladdened by the enthusiasm of the Florents.

Lord Florent announced privately to family at the Foxhole during breakfast that negotiations
were complete and that Alekyne was officially betrothed to Lady Dacey Mormont. Stannis
was preparing to leave for the Red Keep afterwards, except that there was a lone lurking
figure at the corner of his eye.

Merrell, the quietest, most sneaking-est Florent yet, was standing behind him. It was years of
being used to Merrell’s ways that prevented Stannis from startling when he turned and
discovered he was being stared at. Merrell was being a creepy unblinking statue again.

It was in his nature to be beneath notice and Selyse absolutely encouraged this; he was the
strange child who thought it fun to sit and regulate his breathing and when playing Murder,
the disconcerting habit of falling onto the ground with his limbs splayed out and then going
so still as to merit second looks for appearing so dead. (He’d terrified poor Sam more than
once by simply posing dead in random rooms, waiting for anybody to enter.) He was an
ambush player; whereas Imry and the others liked to actively hunt, he would seek out
alcoves, side chambers, large doors to hide behind and wait. He waited, almost always one of
two last ones left by evening, and if the other player was unlucky enough to wander past his
perch, he’d have the drop on them. Throatstab, throatstab, throatstab.

Stannis vaguely worried about when Merrell would grow up enough to have the strength and
mass to start training at garrots.

“What is it?” Stannis asked.

“You need to speak to Renly.”

“What about?”

“He’s angry. I don’t want to get punched in the face. On accident. When I surprise him.”

Stannis frowned; Renly did not often show his temper. Everybody had given up on getting
Merrell to at least have audible footfalls. He was getting better at approaching people to the
side instead of from behind, but Imry was always encouraging him otherwise.

“Where is he?”

“The training yard.”

Well. Stannis would see him and then go. He could afford to be a little late for once to Small

always startled Stannis; he was as elusive as a shadow. He walked to the training yard and
Renly was wildly whacking away at a sandbag with a training hammer, grunting and snarling

Stannis watched him and saw it true, that Baratheon fury in all its futile violence, a state that

“Renly,” he called out.

hard. He lifted a hand to wipe at his eyes.

“Renly,” Stannis approached.

“I apologize,” Renly bit out. “I’m having a stupid emotion and I lost control.”

“Better the sandbag than somebody else,” Stannis said. “Do you wish to speak of it? Why did

Renly’s jaw worked and Stannis reached out to put his hand there as Selyse did for him.

“... He’s getting married.”

Stannis blinked at Renly and Renly stood, silent and watchful.

“It’s stupid,” Renly muttered, stepping away from him.

“No,” Stannis could not help the bark in his voice. “Renly. Young fancies are. Normal.”

“You are my little brother and I love you,” Stannis finally said, stymied. “So. Whatever it is.

“Young fancies are normal,” Stannis repeated himself. “You will not always feel this way

He stepped back himself, and took a deep breath through his nose.

“The Dornish Vice,” Renly sneered in response. “How can Stormlanders rally to a Lord

Renly nodded after a moment of consideration.

“Selyse would say that,” Renly made a wobbly smile.

Stannis swallowed.

“You were always there. You weren’t fun. You didn’t let me put off lessons. You didn’t let me

“You are my big brother and I love you,” Renly said with firm finality.

Renly took a step back, to go pick up the hammer and they took their leave of each other for

Queen Cersei’s water broke in the middle of the night while she was in a dreamwine sleep.
She thrashed and cried out, the pain waking her at last and a flurry of panicked activity
began. She expected it to be like last time; for Pycelle to be called in, and her handmaids to
be useless lumps surrounding her. She was not expecting Robert to come striding in, stinking
of vinegar and wearing a smock. He made orders and humiliatingly, she was stripped out of
her nightgown and servants were wiping at her with vinegar. She could not understand the
purpose of it, but she was in too much pain to resist. Her hair was hastily braided and pinned
out of the way and a cap tied over it. A smock was put on her and shamefully it did not even
come over the tops of her thighs, she was so big. To more of her shock, Robert picked her up
and began marching out of her chambers.

“Put me down! Arrrgh! What is the meaning of this! Oaf!”

“Getting you to the proper birthing chamber, of course!” Robert said.

“You-! What-!”

“Don’t worry, I won’t drop you!”

That was not what she was concerned about. She could see Jaime striding after them and it
was good to have him there. Robert stopped in front of an unfamiliar chamber of the Red
Keep and put her down. She had no choice but to waddle into the so called birthing chamber.
Robert followed her and shut the door on Jaime.

It was dreadful. Bare of anything, with some strange, metal chair-table covered in a sheet that
looked more a dungeon’s torture device than anything a laboring woman would want. The
room reeked of vinegar.

“I am not staying here!” Cersei tried to stand tall, but another spasm of pain prevented her
from doing so.

“But it’s clean!” Robert replied, waving his hands. “Safer for everybody and you will have
less risk of infection! Can’t risk birthing bed fever!”

Cersei rolled her eyes and was forced by another contraction to lay on her side on the metal
chair-thing. It was cold! She hated it!

She could hear the wavering voice of Pycelle coming from behind the door. Robert stood up
and opened the door only long enough to stick his head out and informed Pycelle that by
order of the King, he was not to come in until he had disinfected himself with soap and
vinegar and to get a fresh pair of robes. Preferably a smock, as they were for sure clean.
Pycelle sputtered, but Robert shut the door on him. They were left alone again.

“Why are you still here!?” Cersei growled.

“Stannis was with Selyse. So I will be here too. I ought to have been for Joffrey, but I wasn’t.
This time, I’m doing it right.”

Oh, gods, curse him and his stupid brother and their stupid competitions! Who needed a great
big lump in the room while laboring!?

“I don’t need you! I don’t need anybody!”
Robert, under the impression that her ill temper was the understandable consequence of pain,

“Pyclle will be back. In the meantime, I will wait.”

“You’ll wait hours, even a day? Hah!” Cersei barked at him the way he’s barked that stupid
laugh at her.

“I’m not afraid of blood and pain,” Robert nodded. “I will wait. Perhaps this time will not be

Cersei made another inarticulate sound of rage.

Cersei wanted to throw something at him, but it appeared that there is nothing in this room

“I’m cold.”

Robert went to the lone other table in the room and picked up a cotton sheet. It is big enough
to fold several times to drape over her shoulders. Cersei sniffed. Robert returned to his seat.
Cersei supposed he was regretting saying he’ll stay, after all; he’s begun tapping his toes and
fidgeting.

“Oh, how you can wait,” Cersei sneered.

“Will you not take some turns about the room with me? Light exertion may help move things

the Lord Hand!) met in Selyse’s parlor, the furniture was pushed to the side and padded
cotton mats laid out. From there, dressed simply in tunics and loose short trousers, they did
morning exercises that Maege had never seen before; mostly laying on the mats. She
wouldn’t have thought such exercise counted, but even she felt burn as they did leg lifts and
curls and what Selyse called The Hundred. This was all well and good but boring.

And then Maege found out that they played soccer and hammerball! Well! That was more
like it. Not at all like a good spar but definitely worked up a sweat. She observed that there
were scant few other ladies at King’s Landing who ventured to join the Florents in their
games. Maege expected some ill willed gossip about the matter. There were some mutterings,
but Maege quickly learned that the cackling, earthy, unapologetically lusty-about-her-
husband Selyse of the Foxhole was not what Lady Selyse showed to court. In court she
adopted a cordiality with a sheen of iciness, her face smoothed to studied neutrality. She
was… cautious. And Maege was canny enough to understand that this was necessary, that
something somehow about the Royal court put her on guard. That did not mean that she or
Delena had changed in particular; it was merely that they held their tongues and tamped
down their emotions. Other than the common gossip about the more robust than usual sexual
relations with her husband, there was an air of unimpeachable correctness about the Lady
Selyse, kept from being seen as completely boring by Selyse’s enjoyment of dancing and
singing.

Maege and Dacey talked about it as they worked on the maiden cloak and wedding dress. As
far as they could observe the Florents took measures to avoid the notice of the Queen. Not the
King. Not the Hand. Just the Queen. They could not see why, unless it was by avoiding
Cersei they also avoided the notice of Lord Tywin. It seemed to make sense, as far as any
Southron court nonsense made sense to Maege and Dacey. The Florent women made sure to
subordinate themselves to Queen Cersei, were careful of what they said about her at court
itself, and never made their gowns as flashy as hers nor tried to vie with her with their
jewelry. Dacey revealed that even though Cersei was known to approach the King with
various appointments for Westermen nobles at court, no Lannister yet sat at the Small
Council nor any of their more notable bannermen. And after learning who was actually on the
Small Council it was interesting that the Florents had not pushed for more than Ser Axell’s
position as a bureaucrat within the Master of Coin’s offices.

Maege thought it a wise sort of caution, herself. It wouldn’t do to fail at learning the lessons
about overreaching ambitions when it came to Reacher families as the Hightowers. And one
of theirs was Queen once! Jorah and Maege discussed this; it was clear that Dacey was being
politely blocked from full knowledge of Florent doings until after her marriage. Was this
something that would bode ill?

Jorah reminded Maege of the gifts bestowed upon Bear Island. There was a levelheaded
generosity, not foolish openhandedness as old Lord Tytos Lannister. No gold, but supplies
that they sorely needed. If they squandered such gifts it would be only to their detriment.
Everything they did made sense, Jorah thought. Surely the only secrets were on how much
and how far they were along on their various inventions and research; and for that he would
not blame them for secrecy when Dacey could call off the wedding up until the official final
words of the traditional vows.

The guest list was daunting. Delena’s friendship with Lady Lysa meant that the Lord Hand
himself would be in attendance. King Robert had to regretfully decline, as it would not do
that have both the King and Lord Hand out of the court at the same time. It was well,
however, because of course Lord Stannis and Lord Renly would be in attendance, which
meant some of the more prominent Crownlands Houses would also be attendance, and
Stormlands banners as well, trying to be more acquainted with Lord Renly. Of course Lord
Tyrell as Lord Paramount was invited and where he went, it could be expected that his
mother would harangue Redwynes and Hightowers to go also, to show strength. Which
would be countered by the presence of Lord Tarly and the more warsome marcher lords. On a
more familial and pleasant note, the Royces would be making the trip; Alekyne wished for
Selyse, Melessa, and Rhea to sing at the ball.

Jorah and Maege carefully sent out ravens. Lord Stark was invited, though there was
certainly no hope of him making an appearance, not when he was not at the Ship Launch. But
it would not do to simply not do so. Lord Glover was invited as was proper for goodkin to the
family. Various other mountain clan nobles were invited, as they did provide daughters for
marriage to the Mormonts and vice versa in the past. Not so grand as the guests from the
Florent side, but humble and familiar. It would have to do.

Dacey and Maege were making the finishing touches to Dacey’s maiden’s cloak one
afternoon when Lady Lysa bustled into Selyse’s parlor, holding a raven message in her hand.

“Selyse! Oh, Selyse, I have such news!”

She handed it to Selyse, who began to read. Maege and Dacey looked on.

“Huh.”

Lysa had gracefully collapsed into a chair looking excitedly out of sorts.

“Isn’t it awful?” she asked.

“Lord Hoster,” Selyse looked at Maege and Dacey. “Wishes to announce the happy news of a
betrothal for his son Edmure to Lady Lynesse Hightower.”

“Oooh!” Lysa exclaimed. “It’s spite, that’s what that was! I don’t think she looked so fine as
that during the Ship Launch and she wasn’t a better dancer than Delena! But there were ever
so many Hightowers there and Edmure probably let himself get boxed in, the foolish boy!
I’m ever so disappointed!”

Selyse was silent, drumming her fingers on the arm of her chair.

“Lord Hoster’s choice is not foolish,” she concluded. “And considering the contentiousness
of Riverlands lords, a bride from outside with a rich a dowry as a Hightower was quite the

“Delena would do,” Lysa sniffed. “She’s sensible! Oh, you’ve seen the richness of those

“Or, cause for Lord Hoster to take improving the income of his holdings more seriously than

“Perhaps,” Lysa sighed. “It’s just… Edmure wouldn’t heed me! Father was always making

“Stannis and Renly do,” Lysa replied. “I don’t, but I shan’t go out of my way to aid them,

“We would prefer that Tyrells are not… obstacles in the way. But, seeing as Lord Mace is

“Oh, tosh, Selyse,” Lysa giggled.

“Even a fool for a Lord Paramount has his uses,” Selyse grinned.



The wedding at Brightwater Keep was splendid. Let Lord Florent and Lady Selyse ponder
the ramifications of the marriage alliances of the high lords. For Alekyne and Dacey, this day
was one of hope and joy for the both of them.

Jorah grasped Dacey’s hand before leading her towards the Heart Tree, taking a few moments
to gruffly say that had he a daughter, he would have hoped she would be as fine a woman as
Dacey grew up to be. She smiled and kissed his cheek before placing her hand to his elbow
and they began walking out.

The assembled lord and ladies were waiting at the Heart Tree.

“Who comes before the Old Gods?” Lord Alester Florent called out.

“Dacey, of House Mormont,” replied Jorah. “comes here to be wed. A woman grown,
trueborn and noble. She comes to beg the blessing of the Gods. Who comes to claim her?”

“Alekyne, of House Florent, heir to Brightwater Keep. Who gives her?”

“Lord Jorah of House Mormont, who is her uncle.”

“Lady Dacey, do you take this man?” Alester asked.
“I take this man!” Dacey called out, her voice strong.

She stepped forward to Alekyne. He undid the clasp to her cloak and lifted it off, passing it to
Jorah. He undid his cloak, so very finely made out ermine, to drape securely over her
shoulders. They held hands, facing the Heart Tree. The quizzical face looked down upon

in prayer.

“Live long and prosper,” Selyse whispered under her breath.
            Chapter 43: King's Landing: Changes Upon Changes

   King’s Landing was now in a constant state of construction. As each of the Gates were
   excavated and the wildfire removed, the Florents convinced Robert that he might as well
   improve King’s Landing properly.

   An aqueduct begun up the Blackwater Rush, that would cross through the lands of multiple
   lords, required quite the negotiation by Lord Hand Arryn, but Jon was more than capable of
   the task. Eventually, fresh water from afar would be piped into King’s Landing and into
   multiple fountains, cisterns, and would feed public bathhouses. The sourcing for stones to
   build the aqueduct itself might have been even more of a challenge and cost, except that
   Selyse carefully suggested to Lysa to write to her kinswoman Lady Shella Whent about
   allowing the Crown to use Harrenhal as a quarry; the stones were all cut to size already and
   easily chipped free from mortar instead of hewn from bedrock. Lady Shella Whent thought it
   reasonable; she did not use more than the bottom floors of two out of the five great towers
   anyway. Too many ghosts. A fair price for the stones was negotiated and furthermore,
   Harrenhal was so massive that the workers themselves could live in a tower’s ground floor as
   they dismantled it from the top.

   King Robert himself campaigned for guard towers that also were semaphore towers to be
   built alongside the aqueduct, since they did not lack for cut stones, for the posting of rotating
   troops of Gold Cloaks to patrol the aqueduct, even into Riverlands territory. It was argued
   that it would be foolish to not prepare for attempts to illegally tap into and poach the water or
   potential sabotage during future wars. As the aqueduct served the people of King’s Landing,
   it was right that there should be King’s Landing men to patrol it. Robert understood clearly
   the vulnerability of an aqueduct to concentrated siege weapons fire.

   The old Queen’s Fountains were also refurbished. And here, even Robert was aghast at what
   was discovered once the workers began excavating, following the flow of water. Originally,
   only particularly licensed inns or laundries could tap into the flow of water that entered these
   fountains to ensure adequate water levels. It was found that over time various private citizens
   and entities had illegally tapped into the water, taking them from the commons and then also
   having the gall to flush soapy washwater into what was supposed to be drinking water or
   even waste. No wonder the fountain waters were unfit for drinking! But drink from the
   fountains the small folk of King’s Landing must.

   News was freely spread of these terrible lawbreakers and punishments were levied and these
   illegal connections were closed off.

   Selyse scoffed at the idea of merely four fountains being adequate for the growing city. The
   original four cisterns that fed the fountains were well maintained through tradition and their
   locations uphill made for adequate pressure. After investigating and learning from local
   elders that the Queens Fountains never dried up, it was judged that joining up subsidiary
   cisterns to the fountains would not be necessary at this time. The original four fountains were
traditional circular basins with central spouts emerging from statues; marble likenesses of
Good Queen Alysanne held water vessels that were perpetually pouring water.

The basins were changed from their formerly simple layout. Each fountain now had three
different basins. The first was freshest and for taking drinking water from. The second caught
the overflow of the first basin and was oblong in shape and allowed for passing horses, oxen,
or other livestock to drink, and finally the last basin was for smallfolk to rinse soapy laundry,
with sloped, carved ridged interior side walls that allowed for even the poorest persons to
adequately scrub their clothes.

Newer cisterns were built on the hills of King’s Landing. Until the aqueduct was completed,
they would be filled over time with rainwater.

The old existing sewer and drainage system from Jaehaerys I was getting cleared and cleaned
out, and slowly being expanded. This was judged necessary to prevent flooding and turning
the streets into mud and muck by the hooves of livestock and horses churning manure into
the dirt as they passed. As these sewer lines were built out, with many streets being dug up
and opened, new drinking water fountains were installed to the new cisterns. The new
fountains were not the open basin types of the old Queen’s Fountains. Instead, they were
simple, cast iron faucets that had a constant, small stream of water. Enough to quickly cup
your hands under for a drink, or wash your hands or face. People could take buckets or
pitchers to collect their daily water. The many new little fountains being installed in new
places throughout the city, were very welcome.

Thoros of Myr was also useful in that Alekyne befriended him and gave him access to such
finer quality Reach wines (in moderation) such that he would freely move amongst the Essosi
delegations and feigning his usual drunkenness and pretending to doze off in their vicinity,
overhear their discussions in Valyrian and report back. There was news of unrest, which
Alekyne passed on to Stannis. Stannis took note and waited in Small Council for Varys to
report on the growing distrust from the delegates or not. When Varys does his job, it was a
good opportunity to have Robert concerned about more improvements to the Royal Fleet to
make ready against incursions from pirates or sellsails. Which meant more recruits for Robert
to train and oversee (keeping him well motivated and physically fit) and more troops of
Marines for Stannis to deploy, and more funding for more ships and weapons and generating
more demand for the tin jarred provisions. Profits of which get fed into the ever growing
Florent enterprises. Which were working more and more to tip the balance against the Essosi
in a trade war they were completely unprepared for.

Tyrion, Alekyne, and Selyse worked together and before he left for Casterly Rock, they
finalized a water flushing jake. Selyse privately gave some clue to Stannis of her previous life
as a smallfolk; she mentioned that it was actually very lucky that she had experience living in
an apartment with a negligent landlord, which rather forced her to make small home repairs
by herself. Including a malfunctioning toilet, which was her word for the thing. So she knew
entirely how it ought to be built.

Tyrion was only on the part where he could tap into the various existing water pipes
connecting to cisterns built long ago at the very top of the Rock, that caught rainwater, in
order to install faucets where one could fill a bucket and tip water down the jake to move
waste along. He had the idea to use the principles of siphoning and liquids blocking air, so he
would use a bowl with a s-bend pipe extending out the bottom. It prevented stink rising up
from the existing jakes and one could just pour in more water into the bowl and the siphon
action would suck the waste out. And then you’d have to replace water to previous levels to
block off the s-pipe once more. It was serviceable, but needed a little more finessing.

It was a very good start indeed. Selyse added a small cistern attached to the bowl, with a
flush valve to release water into the bowl directly after use and a fill valve to refill the little
cistern and would stop the inflow of water with a glass float to turn it off at sufficient fill
level. Alekyne had his workshop throw together a working prototype and it was a go. Once
Tyrion finished his work remediating the pipes and sewers at Casterly Rock, Lord Arryn
wanted him to see to getting a sufficient number installed at the Eyrie. If any other castle in
the Westeros could do with flushing jakes instead of chamber pots, it was the Eyrie. Robert
was convinced to have the Red Keep entirely renovated with flushing jakes; he certainly
wanted his immediate environs as stink-free as possible.

Which meant that as a form of fashion and comfort, as well as sanitation, the Flushing Jake
was worth establishing factories for, as well as an entire new network of merchants and
plumbers for the business. The people of King’s Landing were very used to collecting their
urine and waste in barrels by now, however. The poorest smallfolk of Fleabottom even
benefited by a guaranteed few pennies a day for the contents of their overnight chamber pots.
There were a few enterprising urine collectors who saw the worth in getting full barrels as
quickly as possible and going into Fleabottom and paying pennies to fill them up and then
setting out by afternoon to their client fulling mills outside of King’s Landing.

The sheer size of the Florent interests is almost beyond Stannis’ abilities to keep track, so
wide a net they are weaving. It was getting so that they had to hire executive officers for each
of their associated companies and interests; educated men from lower Houses or even well
established merchant families. Especially experienced merchant families who knew by
experience the worth of a profit and loss statement and who grasped immediately the value of
double-entry bookkeeping.Tyrion was correct in his analysis of what the Florents were
planning to do in regards to the fabrics industry. Only he could not possibly know the scope
of otherworldly dimensional knowledge that Selyse spent years writing down that she was
now able to reverse engineer using the time and funds of the Florent enterprises.

Selyse had brainstormed alone for days, ransacking her accumulated notebooks in the
Foxhole for anything she could remember about player pianos, music boxes, and punch cards
for the computers from ‘Hidden Figures’ and ‘Desk Set’. From this, she came up with punch
cards to ‘program’ patterns for looms to weave. She set Rhea on the task and her cousin did
not disappoint. First came the looms capable of weaving polka-dotted patterns out of Rhea’s
workshop in Runestone. The patterns were new and charming and declared stylish and
quickly entered into merchants’ hands.

And since she had figured out how music boxes worked anyway… King’s Landing
introduced music boxes, where new small factories began to be set up to preserve the shorter,
more popular tunes for later listening entertainment. The boxes themselves came in great
variety. The cheapest examples were plain wooden boxes. If one had more coppers to spend,
one could have painted boxes or carved lids. Inlay patterns became popular and if one was
very bent on showing off, you could have yours made out of metal and decorated with jewels
or filigree as you liked and could have interchangeable song cylinders at that!

Erren in the meantime was taking hanks of cotton and wool threads and boiling them in all
sorts of substances, just to see what would happen. He hit upon boiling cotton threads in a
solution of lye that resulted in better dye acceptance and a sheen that was almost satin-like.
The dyed cotton cloth from this was cheaper than satin, but attractive and once again, fueled
by new dresses worn by Lady Lysa and Selyse and ladies at court who followed their lead,
reported upon in the King's Landing Spectator, caused a boom in demand from the
dressmakers and tailors serving nobles and the richer merchants and tradespeople from
King’s Landing to Lannisport, from Oldtown to White Harbor. This set the dyer’s guilds at
Brightwater Keep’s holdings ablaze with activity.

Rhea’s ambition was such that immediately after she could get her hands on sufficient
amounts of Errenized spools of thread, she produced a brocade, based on a pattern that
Delena drew out, commissioned by Selyse. Brocade! Produced in a matter of weeks using a
programmed, waterwheel-driven loom running day and night when normally such rich fabric
took the better part of a year, and made from imported Essosi silk at great cost! Selyse
craftily asked Delena to draw out a pattern that would appeal to the likes of the Lannisters.
Selyse would critically eye the sketches Delena gave her, muttering to herself mysterious
phrases such as, ‘More. More Versace. Dolce and Gabbana all up in here. Baroque up the
wazoo. More!” and the results were muscular leonine feline shapes leaping or lounging
amongst wreaths of fern and leaf fronds, flowers, and ostentatious curlicues, blaring yellows
on red. Rhea nearly set out to visit the Foxhole in person from Runestone to yell at Selyse for
commissioning such a thing that had her nearly cross-eyed punching out the pattern on cards.

But the results were incontestable. The fabric looked rich! Bolts of it were produced and
Robert gifted them to Cersei with great aplomb. She was enamored and made use of it
immediately, for a new cloak and matching gown and finally found herself reported in the
King's Landing Spectator, to her immense gratification; she had privately thought whoever
was doing the Spectating didn’t know proper taste at all, concentrating mainly on Lady Lysa
and Lady Selyse! Tyrion would laugh to himself once he saw the bolts showing up at
Casterly Rock, where fist fights nearly broke out amongst his family to get their hands on a
cloth that was finally good enough for them; no mere stripes, dots, zigzags, or herringbones!
He allowed for a cloak of it to be fashioned for himself; can’t be seen as not being
fashionable, after all. He much preferred going about in his solid color Florent Jackets. Even
Tywin could not resist; he took lengths of the brocade to be used as a sash and as a fresh
lining to his favorite cloak. Otherwise, the brocade bolts were so many, so wide and long, that
they could fashion pillows, curtains, bedspreads, even upholster furniture with the stuff!
Tyrion could picture Alekyne cackling and rubbing his hands together at the way the
Lannisters at large were clamoring for his House’s product. What surely was best of all is the
knowledge that the Lannisters didn’t know where the cloth came from. Most nobility didn’t;
they commissioned clothing through private dressmakers and tailors, who bought bolts from
drapers, who in turn bought from large warehouses of other middlemen situated in the Reach.

When Lord Alester and his wife Lady Melara had cause to visit Highgarden and schmooze
with the Reacher lords who were closer to the Tyrells at a tourney, he arrived with a Florent-
special brocade cloak and Melara with a brocade sash and insets to her gown; gamboling
foxes on fields of flowers and leaves. Unlike the Lannister need for showiness, Lord Alester
much preferred Selyse’s sense of chic by using different shades of blue instead for the whole

the bespoke pattern; did they have Essosi contacts and found commission with weavers in the

Lord Alester dramatically had a troop of liveried servants enter Highgarden’s main hall with
bolts of brocade in their arms that would seduce the Tyrells; in lush greens and yellows, some

“A gift,” Lord Alester purred at the Tyrells. “A demonstration of how superior Westerosi

They snapped it all up, hook, line, and sinker. All the lords present began asking how to get
their own brocades of such make.

Entire new, once again, heavily guarded weaving factories sprang up at Brightwater Keep,
Horn Hill, and Runestone, specializing in brocades. Soon enough Delena began to need
subordinate artists of her own to fulfill the commissions from various noble Houses, who
would refine the sketches and send the drawings to the brocade factories, where specialized
laborers converted them onto punch cards for the looms to work on. Selyse also wisely
helped her design innocuous brocades with slightly simpler leaves, flowers, birds, butterflies,
and curling ribbons or braid patterns to produce for the merchant and tradespeople smallfolk
who read the King's Landing Spectator aspirationally, wanting to know and copy the latest
court styles.

The punch card mechanism of course also worked for larger, heavy-duty wool looms and
soon enough, with the better grades of steel coming from the Royal steelworks, they would
engineer a gripper system to pluck up weft to allow sharp steel blades to cut a tufted pile.
Westerosi carpets entered the markets to immediate popularity. This time, Storm’s End got
first crack at setting up the factory as wool mills were already at work, thanks to Renly taking
his future seat as Lord of Storm’s End seriously. They did not attempt to copy the truly fine
detail and make of Myrish carpets; they went for robust geometric patterns that appealed to
the more practical and simple tastes of the Stormlands. Which also appealed to the tastes of
Northerners. Which was the big, untapped market that the Florents were raring to charge into.
The Manderlys quickly moved into position and with their connections with the Woolfields,
entered into licensing contract agreements (Selyse crowed at the acceptance of the idea by the
practical Northerners) and began setting up Florent-style wool mills and factories, managed
by senior trained workers sent on by the Florents. Carpets remained a Storm’s End exclusive
for now, but it was sensible to have North-made woolen yarns and cloth widely available.

The Myrish delegates were howling with indignation once the laceworks got set up. They
were not so fine in make of course, but what did it matter, when they were so cheap! It was
slower to spread the trend for frothy lace-edged nightgowns, chemise, petticoats, and small
clothes amongst noble ladies and then onwards into the growing merchant class of smallfolk
of the harbor cities (since it was untoward to represent such things in print for advertisement),
but once it happened, it sealed a market that Myr could not enter. Eventually, the cheap
Westerosi lace would edge commoners’ handkerchiefs, become doilies and tablecloths, and
other common household fabric trims. The Myrish were so distressed that they demanded
that the factories churning out imitation carpets, lace, and other such stuffs be shut down as
theft of Myrish works. King Robert boomed back at them that there could not be any such
theft; these Westerosi-made products were clearly simpler, dare he say, not as luxurious in
make as true Myrish work. What could they have to complain of? The local small merchant
wanting a warm carpet underfoot in his bedroom would never have afforded a Myrish carpet
anyway!

They had no ready answer for that. They had no idea the value of sheer volume at lower price
points. Not like Selyse.

The other Essosi representatives (except for the Braavosi) were very nervous indeed. The
only relief was that there couldn’t possibly be any way that the spices, tea, and silks
particularly of the east could be replicated in Westeros. Selyse privately snickered to Stannis
after a report by Thoros; she knew the secret of silk very well.

“If you want to really set off a war with Essos, have Robert pay Varys to send infiltrators into
Yi Ti. Have them steal silkworm eggs.”

“Silkworm?” Stannis raised an eyebrow.

“Yes. Larvae of the silk moth. They feed only on mulberry leaves and their cocoons are the
thread that is silk. Of course, if Yi Ti is like the civilization that first cultivated silk of my
world, they do not hesitate to kill those who would enter the silkworm farms to steal the
cocoons. Of course. They were worth their weight in gold.”

“The effort would distract from the War, then.”

“Yes.”

By the time the Acclaim returned from Braavos, with spices and tea, Erren was already
making the Florents a new favorite with the Redwynes, indeed. Sulfur powder sprayed upon
growing grapes got rid of powdery mildew, saving harvests. Of course Redwyne ships began
going directly to Dragonstone for the sulfur mined there. For fairness (and more profits for
Dragonstone), the technique was released to the Dornish as well. The boom in grape yield set
the stage for Erren to publish and spread the news and great potential of distilling wine for
more complicated liquors. Of course Bellflower Press was also doing brisk business selling
books on how to get more compost for increasing crop yields faster with biogas digesters and
the benefits of harnessing the methane for cooking. The friendly competition between these
winemaking regions flared up as they began competing on brandies and cognacs, fine enough
to whet the tastes of Essosi. Needless to say, the Tyroshi delegates were most put out that
their pear brandy had such competition.

The success of the Acclaim legitimized the Iron Islands Trading Company. Lord Rodrik
immediately petitioned Stannis to release certain better navigation instructors from the Royal
Fleet to establish a school at Harlaw to teach reading, writing, and mathematics as a
foundation for teaching navigation, which was speedily approved. The school was filled
quickly by aspiring Ironborn youngsters, entranced by the tales of fine sailing from the
returning crew and the crowing of Aeron Greyjoy. Yara and Theon were enrolled themselves.
The Royal Shipyard went to work, building out sister ships to the Acclaim.

The Acclaim set out once again laden with Florent cloth stuffs, Vale glass, Stormlands
carpets, Lannister clocks, (Delena designed a rather adorable rounded lionhead logo for
Tyrion’s workers to stamp on the bottoms of the clocks, a lion with satisfied closed eyes as if
purring and a smiling mouth), King’s Landing music boxes, and Iron Island cameos, mother-
of-pearl trinkets and pearls. Sophisticated Braavosi went mad for the merchandise; the
Westerosi make guaranteed slave-free sourcing and it was all so much cheaper than expected
for the quality. The Braavosi delegates were only too happy to be invited to the private
dinners with Lord Hand Arryn, where he was carefully getting to know the Gulltown Arryns
and discussed what would also be pleasing to the Braavosi markets.

By the time a new Master of Coin was named, a Hugh Arryn, Selyse settled on something
none of the Free Cities were capable of producing themselves. Porcelain. These delicate
translucent ceramics were imported at great cost from Yi Ti and as yet the only examples she
had seen up close herself were a set of cups in the Red Keep that dated to the time of Corlys
Velaryon, so rare were the intact specimens. As there were glassworks already within the
Vale, the Arryns and Royces would oversee the factories. The mountains of the Vale revealed
their own white gold; kaolin clay was available for mining and already powders of
feldspathic rocks were used in glassmaking. New mines opened and kilns were being
prepped. The Florents expected to have a time of experimentation; Selyse did not know the
correct ratio of kaolin to feldspar herself, nor the correct firing temperature or duration. She
did know, however (and as shown by the Yi Ti porcelain examples) that cobalt would make a
beautiful blue for decoration before firing. A call for skilled potters went out and Selyse
expected an industry as great as Meissen or Sèvres to emerge given time.

Alekyne finally made his breakthrough, beating out Erren in regards to the tin jars: he
designed machines capable of making the double seam interlock between a tin can body and
lid. Dacey was quite bemused by the howling, fist pumping, and jumping up and down of the
Florents at the Foxhole over the matter. Even Stannis was excited, though he expressed this
by silently smiling all the way with both sides of his mouth. From there, the Florents could
produce absolute industry game changers in food preservation. Obviously, they also funded
the opening of a can opener factory. The existing tin jarring factory would still make jars and
lids; they would be sold for civilian use for private canning or as receptacles for all sorts of
household and kitchen goods, as they were rodent and vermin proof. A second proper tin can
factory would be built and opened.

Canned baked beans were immediately added to the supplies for the Royal Fleet. Evaporated
milk was immediately popular and released for civilian purchase, after sufficient quantities
were distributed to the Royal Fleet supply depots. Milk usually had to be sold in a day and
the herds immediately around King’s Landing produced bad milk from poor quality fodder.
The milk often required adulteration to make it look more like milk. It was sold in bulk in
open barrels in crowded, open air markets and transported to market in uncovered containers
on the back of a horse-drawn wagon, exposed to road dust. It made people sick more often
than not. Milk with a shelf life of months, perhaps a year, clean, of better quality? Sold with
great clamor when available.
Finally, sliced fruit could be added to the meals of sailors of the Royal Fleet. Selyse had
Stannis to convince Robert to order Pycelle to send out ravens to all the North and Iron
Islands Houses, to inquire as to the fruits they most missed during winters. Rhea happily
conducted full immersion boiling bath tests and they began rolling out canned peaches and
cherries, which were of course made available for Northern and Iron Islands markets.

All this was well and good, but did not satisfy Selyse.

The fact of the matter was that there was a limit to how well they could make steel with the
heat of charcoal or even coal. Tobho Mott’s skills with access to waterwheel power were
formidable, but Selyse was often heard to say that ‘Quantity has a Quality all its own’.
Stannis could only imagine that she meant to arm and armor each and every able-bodied man
in Westeros. The amount of steel that would require was beyond his imagination. Yet, it was
as simple and difficult as that.

Alekyne had experimented so extensively with his steel wheeled bow that Selyse and he
came to the conclusion that it was simply too rigid and heavy for prolonged use in wartime
situations. If he, who had multiple prototypes made to his personal specifications, could not
tolerate the fatigue in his arms that came from holding the bow, it would not do, despite the
clear advantages of range, accuracy, and speed of arrow flight. When on the hunt, his arrows
were quite perilous against deer that didn’t know what was coming. Selyse was less sanguine
about the chances of getting an obsidian tipped arrow past a White Walker if they couldn’t
literally rain down arrows upon them.

Control was everything; there was a reason why the wildfire was being placed on barges
slowly floated out in the Blackwater Bay at a suitable distance away in the middle of night
and the longest range scorpions the Royal Fleet had would fire flaming bolts at the barges
from a ship to ignite the barge. Stannis saw it as a perfectly acceptable training exercise for
his scorpion crews and a way to toughen them up. Ser Jaime and Thoros had to oversee the
process; it was absolutely too tedious to try disposing of it one gallon at a time, yet they
surely didn’t want a baywide conflagration. So small barges it was, a few barrels at a time.

At absolute worse case scenario, they could use scorpions emplaced at the top of the Wall and
laden with clay pots filled with white phosphorus (White phosphorus was the first new
weapons-grade substance Erren discovered properly by himself after Maester Bryan and
Selyse confirmed the existence of regular phosphorus when she was sixteen) and could just
trust on the white phosphorus to explode and burn with exposure to air by the pots breaking
open on impact. And if that didn’t work, they would just need to use flaming scorpion bolts
to start off and then the white phosphorus would go to work. Stannis was absolutely
frightened that it was due to Selyse’s encouragement that Erren seemed to have discovered
another version of wildfire. Her response was that at least the substance was incapable of
burning water. He was also amazed that Erren produced this substance from essentially
ground up bones. It was the strangest idea that everybody was walking around with that
combustible potential just… integral and inside of them.

More strange than that, Selyse insisted that the substance was a common and important
component of agricultural fertilizers as well in her world. Stannis simply didn’t understand;
that stuff burns in air! Erren would grin at him and shrug; showing Stannis the chemical
  notation for phosphoric acid would be as useful as showing him magical ritual spellbooks
  from Essos.

  They needed more steel. They needed ways to smelt more metals on the periodic table to
  make new alloys; there were tons and tons of tailings from the Iron Islands, Dragonstone,
  from Royce holdings, even Casterly Rock that were judged useless because up to now, there
  was no way to get sustained heat hot enough to unlock the metal within. After discussing
  with Erren and Alekyne, Selyse approached Stannis and informed him that they were simply
  going to have to do what she had not thought necessary until now.

  They were going to harness lightning. Electricity, to reach the higher temperatures required
  for smelting new metals.

  Stannis is very sure it would all end in death and destruction. Selyse made a wry grin and
  said they could only hope. Alekyne just silently rubbed his hands while Erren cackled like the
  fearless maniac who played with dangerous substances that he was. It is most disconcerting.

             Chapter 44: King's Landing: It's a Nameday


“Oooh, Gods be good,” Lysa moaned, shifting to her side. This latest pregnancy was the
furthest along yet and she was cautiously hopeful. Her weight gain was greater than before,
her belly distended further than before. These were all good signs, surely. Take it day by day,
Selyse advised and Lysa tried to do so. To not fret; fretting caused a fear in the blood and the
fear could strangle a growing babe within. She would go to the nearest chapel within the Red
Keep and sit and contemplate The Mother. Not pray. Prayers haven’t done any good in the
past. She sat and breathed slowly and evenly, seeking a feeling of peace. And hope. She
would do this until she was forced by inevitable pregnant necessity to seek out the nearest
privy, whereupon finishing, she would return to her chambers.

As her pregnancy progressed, every kick and movement she felt made her heart leap with
fragile joy. Selyse and Delena visited every day and they went through breathing exercises
together and otherwise kept her company. She was always glad to have Armand over for
visits, to make him cackle with games of peekaboo or tickling his round tummy. At two years
in age, his hair was coming in, solid black tufts haphazardly sprouting at only the back of his
head. This unfortunate hair pattern made his resemblance to Stannis all the greater, though
Lysa would never say so!

Lysa slowly levered herself upright and went to the privy yet again. She sighed, carefully
leaning her elbows on her knees. She was so sleepy…! It was still dark outside. She got up
afterwards and slowly made her way back to her bed. Just as she got in, a familiar, terrible
pain struck.

“Oh-!” she whimpered.

Thirty six weeks-! It’s-! It’s too soon! Oh no!

Tears came to her eyes.

“Oh, oh please!” she began to breathe deeply. “False labor. Please!”

She waited, breathing steadily, listening to the ticking of the clock, her hands clenched in her
blanket. The recurring pulses of pain did not go away, despite her waiting.

Well. She wiped her eyes. Well.

She reached out and tugged on the tassel rope that connected to a servants’ bell.

“Prepare the birthing chamber,” she informed them when they arrived. “I wish for the Head
Midwife Alys to be summoned. I wish for Lady Baratheon and Lady Delena Florent…
notified.”

“Shall we tell Lord Arryn…?”
“It is not as we have hoped,” Lysa said. “And it is very late. Let him sleep. And inform him
in the morning, after this is over.”

She waited. She was changed into a smock, carried by stretcher to the birthing chamber, and
she made her way over to the metal bed and laid on it. She listened to the ticking of the clock.
She felt cold and far away. Breathe.

She looked up when there was a knock on the door. It was her friends! Selyse and Delena
came in, also in smocks. How good it was to see them! They came despite the very late hour!

“Oh!” Lysa teared up.

“Shh, shh,” Selyse went over to take her hand. “It will be alright.”

“Thir- Thirty six-”

“I know,” Selyse nodded, while Delena rubbed her shoulder. “Not ideal. But there is still
hope. Just breathe. Wait for Alys. We’re here with you.”

They waited. Alys and her assistants arrived and checked on Lysa’s dilation. It was not
moving along too fast, judging from Lysa’s memories of when her labor pains began. That
was… That was good. Selyse and Delena kept her company, bringing water for her to sip,
reciting stories to distract her as she waited. She would’ve wanted to move and walk as
Selyse was said to have done, but she was so large that it didn’t feel right. Selyse reminded
her to only do what she wished.

She stayed on her side, while Selyse and Delena took turns rubbing her back.

The pain increased. It was just like all the other times before, only somehow, worse. Lysa
breathed through it. It was the waiting that got to you, just as Selyse said. Let it pass.

Her water broke. That was a terrifying moment. No going back now-!

Alys was kindly and professional as ever.

“There you go,” she said encouragingly. “Just a little longer.”

When it was finally safe to push, Lysa had rolled onto her other side. Selyse was there, seated
at the bedside, with Lysa’s leg braced on her shoulder. Selyse gripped firmly.

“Push when Alys says, alright?” Selyse smiled at her. “You can do it!”

Lysa nodded frantically.

Alys gave the order and Lysa bore down, with Selyse and Delena encouraging her to yell and
breathe as she went. She huffed. She puffed. Delena wiped at her tears and sweat.

“Once more, milady, just got to get the shoulder-”

Lysa yelled.
“FIDDLESTICKS!” she shrieked. “POO!”

Selyse snorted through her nose.

“Come on!” Alys encouraged. “There- There- There-”

“POPPYCOCK!”

Through the haze of pain there was a sudden emptiness. Lysa slumped as Alys and her
assistants busied themselves.

Lysa closed her eyes. Selyse carefully put Lysa’s leg down.

A series of small hiccuping noises caused Lysa to startle.

“Lysa!” Delena gripped her hand.

“It’s alive!” Selyse gripped her other hand.

Lysa burst into fresh tears.

Alys came over.

“Lady Arryn,” she bowed her head, while holding the washed infant out. “You have a son.”

Lysa reached out to hold him, still in a state of bewildered shock.

“Just the afterbirth now,” Selyse said.

Lysa nodded. And then frowned.

“It- It's hurting again. Why-?”

Alys was carefully palpitating Lysa’s belly.

“Twins, milady!”

“...What-!” Lysa gasped.

“Bring that bassinet here,” Selyse ordered. “Has anybody informed Lord Arryn!? Wake him!
Wake him!”

By the time Lord Arryn arrived, Lysa was holding her twins. A boy and a girl.

“My lord husband,” Lysa gave a watery smile.

“My lady wife,” Jon murmured, cautiously entering the room.
Selyse and Delena quickly made way and he went to Lysa’s bedside. He sat down.

The news of Lysa surviving the birth of her twins, Roland and Elyse, filled the Red Keep

He held his finger out to Roland and the infant grasped it.

Roland and Elyse inspired Robert to visit the Royal nursery every day.

He worked on being a more present father to his two sons. He bobbled Eddard. He wanted to

With Joffrey, he gave him big bear hugs, swung him around by the arms or legs or tossed and
